items.title: Species diversity increases information flow about predation in bird communities
items.subtitle: Martínez, Xingfeng Si, Qiang Zhang, Eben Goodale The Biodiversity-Ecosystem Functioning (BEF) literature has shown species diversity to be essential for ecosystem functioning and services.
items.feedText:
Martínez, Xingfeng Si, Qiang Zhang, Eben Goodale

The Biodiversity-Ecosystem Functioning (BEF) literature has shown species diversity to be essential for ecosystem functioning and services. Yet this concept has not been extended often to behavioral ecology, so that although it is understood that acquiring social information from heterospecific individuals is an important component of ecosystem functioning, it is unclear how animal signaling at the community level, and subsequent information flow, is related to i…
items.body: The Biodiversity-Ecosystem Functioning (BEF) literature has shown species diversity to be essential for ecosystem functioning and services. Yet this concept has not been extended often to behavioral ecology, so that although it is understood that acquiring social information from heterospecific individuals is an important component of ecosystem functioning, it is unclear how animal signaling at the community level, and subsequent information flow, is related to increased species diversity. Eliciting vocal responses using predator models across 10 nature reserves on a latitudinal gradient, we first show that the species diversity of birds is correlated with signaling about predation, both in the low-risk system of mobbing and in the higher-risk system of alarm calls. After finding a similar result across a fragment area gradient in one reserve, we used this system to test how interspecific information flow is affected by species diversity. Potential mechanisms behind this effect include that species are complementary in the characteristics of their mobbing calls, so more species translates into more cumulative information, or there are higher signaling rates as more individuals are involved, or a specific keystone species is more likely to occur. This experiment varied the number of species producing mobbing calls (one, two, four, eight species), with two playback construction methods (standardizing call rate, as typical for BEF experiments, or letting it increase with species richness, as in natural assemblages). Heterospecific mobbing participation (number of vocal species, number of participating individuals), and responses (call rate, probability to call in the first minute and frequency range) increased with species richness. Construction method significantly interacted with species richness, as non-standardized exemplars showed accentuated response as species richness increased. These results match expectations that complementary differences among species in the acoustic characteristics of mobbing calls, and increased call rate, both contribute to the result. There was little evidence that the signals of one particular species changed the experimental result. The overall evidence thus supports the hypothesis that the species diversity of a community is a key component influencing the quantity and the characteristics of signaling and information flow inside it.

items.body:
# Bis zu 15 Zentimeter Schnee: Winter trifft Bayern mit voller Wucht

- Startseite
- Panorama
## Bis zu 15 Zentimeter Schnee: Winter trifft Bayern mit voller Wucht – DWD warnt vor allem in zwei Regionen

Stand: 25.11.2026, 08:38 Uhr

Von: Benedikt Strobach

Kommentare Drucken Teilen

Der Winter meldet sich in Bayern zurück: Der Deutsche Wetterdienst warnt vor Neuschnee, Glätte und Dauerfrost. Besonders betroffen sind zwei Regionen.

München – Der Spätherbst verabschiedet sich in Bayern mit sinkenden Temperaturen: Nach teils noch freundlichen Abschnitten zur Wochenmitte setzt sich in der zweiten Wochenhälfte im Freistaat endgültig kalte Luft durch. Ein Ausläufer eines Tiefdruckgebiets über Frankreich nähert sich von Südwesten und sorgt vor allem im Süden und Südosten für unbeständiges und zunehmend winterliches Wetter . Wie der Deutsche Wetterdienst (DWD) in seinen aktuellen Warnlage- und Vorhersageberichten meldet, müssen sich Autofahrer und Fußgänger auf Schneefall, Glätte sowie Frost einstellen.

## Bis zu 15 Zentimeter Neuschnee in Bayern: Schwerpunkt im Süden und Osten

Der Schwerpunkt der nun kommenden winterlichen Niederschläge liegt in den kommenden Tagen im Süden und Osten des Freistaats. Ausgangs der Nacht zum Donnerstag (26. November) setzt an den Alpen und am Bayerischen Wald zunächst leichter Schneefall ein. Im weiteren Tagesverlauf weiten sich die Schneefälle von den mittleren und östlichen Alpen weiter nach Nordosten aus. Bereits zuvor hatte ein Wintereinbruch in Bayern für erste weiße Landschaften gesorgt.

Aktuell gilt bereits eine amtliche Warnung vor Frost in Bayern. Bis 12 Uhr kann laut DWD leichter bis mäßiger Frost bei Temperaturen zwischen –4 und –9 Grad auftreten. Die Meteorologen warnen vor möglichen Frostschäden und empfehlen, gegebenenfalls Frostschutzmaßnahmen zu ergreifen. In den südlichen Landkreisen des Freistaats besteht aktuell bis 9 Uhr auch Gefahr wegen vereinzelter Glätte. Der DWD warnt vor Rutschgefahr und rät Autofahrern, das Verhalten im Straßenverkehr anzupassen.

In den Höhenlagen oberhalb von 800 Metern – insbesondere im Bereich der Alpen, im östlichen Alpenvorland sowie im südöstlichen Niederbayern – rechnet der DWD mit Schneemengen von bis zu fünf Zentimetern. In hohen Staulagen der östlichen Alpen sind sogar bis zu 15 Zentimeter Neuschnee möglich. Auch in den tieferen Lagen zwischen den Alpen und dem Bayerischen Wald rieseln gebietsweise Flocken herab: Hier kalkulieren die Meteorologen mit ein bis zwei Zentimetern Schnee. Weiter westlich, etwa in weiten Teilen Schwabens sowie im nördlichen Oberbayern, bleibt es dagegen am Donnerstag meist trocken, dort fallen kaum Flocken.

In Nordbayern beginnt der Schneefall ebenfalls in den frühen Morgenstunden des Donnerstags am Bayerischen Wald. Im Tagesverlauf rieselt es vor allem in der Oberpfalz leicht, bevor sich der Schneefall in der Nacht zum Freitag gebietsweise weiter ausbreitet.

## Dauerfrost und Glättegefahr: Gefrierende Nässe sorgt für Glätte

Begleitet werden die Schneefälle von spürbar sinkenden Temperaturen. Am Donnerstag stellt sich vielerorts leichter Dauerfrost ein: Die Höchstwerte verharren zwischen –2 und 0 Grad. Lediglich in einigen tiefer gelegenen Regionen Frankens sowie im direkten Umfeld von Donau und Inn klettert das Thermometer örtlich noch auf 1 bis 2 Grad. Auf den Bergen herrscht ohnehin tiefster Winter – auf dem Großen Arber und in den Kammlagen der Mittelgebirge liegen die Werte um –5 Grad, auf der Zugspitze werden bis zu –7 Grad erwartet.

In den Nächten sinken die Werte verbreitet auf –1 bis –6 Grad, in Nordbayern teils bis auf –7 Grad. Durch überfrierende Nässe und den frischen Schnee besteht auf den Straßen und Gehwegen stellenweise Glättegefahr. Wenn Schnee und Eis die Fahrbahnen überziehen, drohen Behinderungen auf den Verkehrswegen, wie bereits frühere Unfälle und Verkehrsbehinderungen im Freistaat gezeigt haben. In den Ost-West-ausgerichteten Tälern der östlichen Mittelgebirge sowie in Föhntälern der Alpen können zudem Windböen mit Geschwindigkeiten um die 50 km/h auftreten.

## Ausblick auf das Wochenende: Frostnächte halten in Bayern an

Zum Ende der Arbeitswoche am Freitag (27. November) bleibt der Himmel über Bayern meist stark bewölkt bis bedeckt. Örtlich fallen noch ein paar Schneeflocken, bevor sich vor allem in Unterfranken im Tagesverlauf längere sonnige Phasen durchsetzen können. Die Höchstwerte erreichen –3 bis 2 Grad.

Am Wochenende präsentiert sich das Wetter zweigeteilt: Während sich in den Tälern und Niederungen oft zähe hochnebelartige Bewölkung hält, scheint in den Alpen die Sonne . Die Temperaturen liegen zwischen –2 und 2 Grad. Die Nächte bleiben eisig kalt: Bei klarem Himmel können die Temperaturen im Süden bis auf –10 Grad fallen. (Quelle: DWD) ( bes )

items.feedText: Therapeutic modulation of the chemokine signaling axis has proven difficult. items.body: Chemokines and their receptors mediate cell migration and coordinate immune responses, while dysregulation can lead to inflammation. Therapeutic modulation of the chemokine signaling axis has proven difficult. Most drug discovery efforts target the receptors, whereas natural regulatory mechanisms modulate immune responses by directly binding to or modifying the chemokine ligands. Despite this insight, development of effective chemokine-directed modulators has remained elusive. Recent advances in de novo protein design offer an unprecedented opportunity to produce high-affinity binders that efficiently block protein-protein interactions. We implemented a computational workflow leveraging the BindCraft platform to generate miniprotein binders against CCL25, the chemokine ligand for the receptors CCR9 and ACKR4, and implicated in inflammatory bowel diseases. The unbiased development results in several miniproteins designed to block the receptor N-terminus from wrapping the chemokine and preventing productive engagement. Thus, these proteins suppress CCL25-mediated effector coupling and halt MOLT-4 lymphoblast migration. Another class of miniprotein, represented by VUP25111, is predicted to bind CCL25 along the chemokine β1 strand and retained receptor binding. This complex inhibited arrestin recruitment to CCR9, but not to ACKR4, indicating receptor specificity. Additionally, G protein recruitment to CCR9 was unimpeded by VUP25111, suggesting that the miniprotein biased the native agonist towards G proteins. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of differentially targeting CCL25 to suppress CCR9 signaling and new tools to resolve the structural basis of chemokine receptor activation and bias.

items.body:
Christie’s has added the UK auction house Dreweatts to its portfolio.

In a statement on Wednesday, Christie’s chief executive Bonnie Brennan said that the auction house has long admired Dreweatts. “Most importantly, our clients collect across categories and at every price point, and together we have the opportunity to provide them with an even broader and more complete level of service. Both businesses will continue to operate much as they do today, while building on their respective strengths and the significant opportunities we see for future growth,” she said.

Dreweatts specializes in single-owner collections and country house sales, ranging from furniture and works of art, old masters, modern and contemporary art, Asian and European ceramics, modern design, jewelry, silver, luxury accessories, clocks and wine. The auction house was founded in 1759 by Thomas Davis, a cabinetmaker, upholsterer and land agent from Abingdon, Oxfordshire. Dreweatts operates its main salesroom from its country house, Donnington Priory, in Newbury, Berkshire, and also has a showroom in London on Pall Mall.

Henry House, chief executive of Dreweatts, said in a statement that under this new arrangement “we can use the additional advantage of one another’s expertise to better serve our buyers and sellers. Dreweatts has had a parent company before, which enabled us to grow the business and prosper, and this move is an extension of that model.” He added that the Christie’s acquisition provides certainty for the auction house and that Dreweatts will continue, under his and chairman Will Richards’ stewardship.

Christie’s president of EMEA, Anthea Peers, said that the François Pinault-owned auction house recognized Dreweatts as a “healthy, compatible business to our own and the value it can add to what we do for all of our clients.”

On November 19, Dreweatts presented its Fine Watches & Luxury Accessories auction that totaled £529,934 with an 89% sell-through rate. The sale included fine watches, designer handbags, writing instruments and luxury objects from Patek Philippe, Cartier, Hermès, Chanel and Montblanc. The top lots were a Lange & Söhne that sold for £49,780 and a Montblanc black porcelain fountain pen that sold for £8,320.

This average includes polls that ask about support for the Iran War, strikes in Iran, or U.S. military involvement in Iran. Compared with tracking approval ratings, questions about war can be less straightforward. Our goal is to limit the analysis to polls that ask neutral questions rather than introduce assumptions about how the war is going or its objectives. Our default version of the ratings reflects a combination of all polls, whether conducted among adults, registered voters, or likely voters.5

items.body:
# YouTube's iconic iOS app icon may soon return with new customizable icons [Gallery]

- YouTube
## YouTube’s iconic iOS app icon may soon return with new customizable icons [Gallery]

The iconic YouTube app icon that looked like a retro TV found on iOS might be making a comeback, with new customizable icons showing up behind the scenes of a new YouTube update.

In the early days of the iPhone, Apple built a custom app for YouTube on iOS before Google built its own. That included an app icon that looked like a retro TV and it was later replaced when YouTube’s official app launched on the platform.

Now, that icon might be coming back.

Android Authority spotted several new app icons YouTube for Android is testing in its latest beta update (v21.47.483-BETA). These icons seem to be tied to a new feature that would allow users to customize the homescreen icon for YouTube, and includes seven designs in total including two throwback designs. One is the aforementioned retro TV icon used on iOS, which was never on YouTube for Android, and another is an old stacked YouTube logo design.

Users would be able to change the app icon via a new setting in the app near the “Appearance” section, but nothing is live just yet. We also don’t know if this is Android-only, if this is limited to Premium subscribers, or when this might debut.

That said, it’s very fun to get these throwbacks, and we’ll be excited to see this functionality go live.

items.title: What the End of Anonymous Writing Means for Academia
items.subtitle: A reader who asked to remain anonymous (seriously) pointed me to an article about the impending end of anonymous writing.
items.feedText:
Large language models are getting increasingly good at identifying the authors of human-written text. In a preprint, “Frontier models need only one text to unmask its human or AI author,” a team of authors claim that:

Given a single text and a simple zero-shot prompt (no web access, tools, candidate lists, or writing samples), frontier models can answer “who wrote this?” at three increasingly specific levels: (1) whether an AI or human wrote it, (2) if an AI, which lab, and (3) if a human, often exactly who. Th…
items.body:
A reader who asked to remain anonymous (seriously) pointed me to an [article](https://www.theargumentmag.com/p/say-goodbye-to-anonymous-posting?) about the impending end of anonymous writing.

Large language models are getting increasingly good at identifying the authors of human-written text. In a preprint, “[Frontier models need only one text to unmask its human or AI author](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26216),” a team of authors claim that:

> Given a single text and a [simple zero-shot prompt](https://github.com/denizbt/unmasking_authors/blob/main/prompts/RQ3/holistic.txt) (no web access, tools, candidate lists, or writing samples), frontier models can answer “who wrote this?” at three increasingly specific levels: (1) whether an AI or human wrote it, (2) if an AI, which lab, and (3) if a human, often exactly who.

The authors asked LLMs to provide the identity of different kinds of often-anonymous writing, such as peer reviews and internet comments.

Their findings:

> The best-performing model we test is Claude Fable 5.2, which names the reviewer of 56% of private peer reviews and the username behind 31% of recent Reddit comments.

It appears that your writing is more likely to be outed as yours if some previous writing of yours was in an LLM’s training data, or if you a lot of your writing is available online. And once a model becomes familiar with you, your writing is very likely to be identified as yours:

> Even when a text is brand new, a model can identify its writer from what it learned about them elsewhere; i.e., once that knowledge is in the weights, the writer cannot do anything about it. This leaves people with the largest public footprints, such as active social media users or established authors, permanently exposed, since paraphrasing the text does not completely remove the deanonymization risk. Moreover, the set of vulnerable writers expands as models improve… Maintaining anonymity is especially important for peer review. Our private lab review data comes from only six writers, but a study across thousands of private peer reviews is underway.

Having an AI disguise your writing style by paraphrasing your writing does diminish its recognizability somewhat, but not entirely, the researchers report.

One commenter on the paper, Kelsey Piper, [writes](https://www.theargumentmag.com/p/say-goodbye-to-anonymous-posting?), “We’re witnessing a total erosion of the ability to write anonymously online,” though “the process is still incomplete. Not everyone should consider themselves deanonymized yet. But the erosion is happening.”

Regarding peer review, she writes:

> [T]he institution of anonymous peer review does not look like it will hold up any longer. The space of possible reviewers for a given academic article review in a particular discipline is pretty small; stylistic tics are sufficient to confidently distinguish between them.

Suppose the LLMs get quite a bit better at identifying the authors of anonymous text. What would that mean for the future of peer review? Well, while some reviewers have regularly opted to forgo anonymity, that is typically a privilege exercised by the relatively senior and secure members of the profession. I wouldn’t expect many more to join their ranks. Nor would I expect academia to be content relying on the forbearance of, say, curious authors or grant judges, to preserve anonymity.

There are [alternatives to peer review](https://dailynous.com/2022/02/07/why-a-crowd-sourced-peer-review-system-would-be-good-for-philosophy-guest-post/). Will the erosion of anonymity push more branches of academia to embrace these alternatives?

Or will it be a reason to use AIs even more in academia, say, as peer reviewers? After all, recently [one set of researchers found that](https://gking.harvard.edu/files/peerless.pdf):

> AI-generated article reviews are now better, by every measure we could construct, than reviews written by well-compensated human experts and judged to be of unusually high quality by journal editors and authors.

The study was performed on quantitative social science papers, not philosophy papers, but of course this technology is only a few years old; who knows how it might develop, and how rapidly.

Discussion welcome.

**UPDATE:** Shen-yi Liao [provided](https://bsky.app/profile/liao.shen-yi.org/post/3n32y4m2mgs2v) a direct link to [the prompt the researchers used](https://github.com/denizbt/unmasking_authors/blob/main/prompts/RQ3/holistic.txt). Try it on an unpublished piece of your writing. I gave ChatGPT [the prompt and the introductory section of an unpublished talk I wrote](https://chatgpt.com/s/p_6b05bf5973a08191aa93b52e7a43d0ed) a couple of years back and it identified me as the author with.62 confidence. You can read its report [↗ chatgpt.com](https://chatgpt.com/s/t_6b05bff752448191821da26c86cb9f2b). I fed it a referee report I wrote and it returned my name with.55 confidence.

items.body:
# Falsche Spendensammler: Polizei warnt nach zwei Fällen

- KURZMELDUNG · DEUTSCHLAND Vor einem Aldi in Bardowick bittet eine Person eine Frau um eine Spende für Menschen mit Behinderungen. Auf dem mobilen Kartenterminal sieht sie 5 Euro, später fehlen laut Polizei 2.000 Euro auf ihrem Konto. Die Warnung vom 20. November 2026 betrifft diesen Fall vom 30. Oktober und einen zweiten vom 4. November. Die Frau wollte zunächst Bargeld geben, wurde laut Polizei aber zur Kartenzahlung gedrängt. Im zweiten Fall sprach ein vermeintlicher Spendensammler einen Mann nahe einer Sparkasse an. Auch er sah 5 Euro auf dem Terminal und bemerkte später eine Abbuchung über 2.000 Euro. Die Polizeiinspektion Lüneburg/Lüchow-Dannenberg/Uelzen spricht von einer manipulierten Anzeige. Wie die Abweichung zwischen dem sichtbaren und dem abgebuchten Betrag technisch zustande kam, geht aus der Mitteilung nicht hervor. Die beiden Fälle belegen daher keine allgemeine Unsicherheit von Kartenzahlungen. Wer eine verdächtige Abbuchung entdeckt, soll laut Polizei sofort die Bank wegen einer Kartensperre verständigen und Anzeige erstatten. Bei einer spontanen Spendenbitte empfiehlt es sich, die Entscheidung aufzuschieben und die genannte Organisation selbst zu überprüfen. Mimikama berichtete bereits im März 2026 über eine ähnliche Spendenmasche. Ein mobiles Kartenlesegerät bestätigt weder die Identität der sammelnden Person noch den Spendenzweck. Das wiederkehrende Muster ist der Zeitdruck: Wer später über einen selbst geprüften Weg spendet, entzieht der Masche ihre wichtigste Grundlage. items.body:
# Worshipping at the altar of Brendan Gregg

Okay, I am the first to admit that I’m a bit manic with AI. When you are working on a problem that has endless possibilities, it is difficult to constrain yourself to a limited set of features.

Can I just add one more?

I have been amazed at all the fun and useful things that a deterministic VM like Rewind enables. I have been using it to help find heisenbugs , to make profile-guided optimization reproducible , and to make Nix builds bit-reproducible . But the most fun has been using it to understand performance.

Turns out that performance is yet another area where Rewind shines. I have been using it to analyze the critical path of builds.

What is the critical path?

The critical path is the longest chain of dependent work in a program. It is the minimum time that the program can take to complete, regardless of how many resources you throw at it. The only way to make a program faster is to shorten the critical path.

If you worship at the altar of Brendan Gregg, you know he spent years turning performance analysis from a dark art into a science. This is a small offering to him. 🤲

I added a new rewind time command to Rewind that analyzes a recording and tells you where the time went and what would make the run finish sooner. You can drill into any part of that answer and see the source lines responsible for it. It’s like Brendan Gregg’s flame graphs but on steroids for the critical path and with a debugger attached. 1 1 All the ideas for the command are either inspired by or directly influenced by Brendan Gregg’s work . Kneel before Zod!

> Aside: New to Rewind? Start with a flaky build you only catch once and dafuq is a deterministic VM?

Let’s see how it works by analyzing the critical path of a libuv build and test run. The build and test suite takes 78 seconds inside Rewind, and even with 64 cores it still takes 47 seconds. Why?

The usual answer is to look at a CPU profile, and in this case a CPU profile would be almost useless. For two thirds of those 47 seconds, the work the build is waiting on is not computing at all: it is asleep . 💤💤💤

## § Where the time goes

Every rewind time starts with two numbers:

$ rewind time 7a29e716 libuv-1.51.0 78.0 s elapsed on the VM's one CPU 47.4 s critical path: the least it can take on any number of CPUs 67% asleep (epoll_pwait 23.1 s, clock_nanosleep 8.53 s, futex 100 ms), 33% computing The first is how long the run took on the VM’s one virtual CPU. The second is the critical path : the longest chain of work where each step had to wait for the one before.

The line under the two numbers applies Gregg’s thread state analysis . Here the biggest state is asleep: 23 seconds in epoll_pwait and 8.5 in clock_nanosleep .

items.body:
# paint in the memory of other programs - citrons.xyz

## paint in the memory of other programs

core is a program that I wrote which spills the viscera of other programs onto the screen and allows you to prod them. it could be called an “esoteric debugger” or a “paint program.”

the visual content of the program is constructed as follows:

- pages of memory (hardcoded for now as 4096 bytes) are arranged on a Z-order curve.
- each page of memory is displayed as a 256x128 rectangle.
- each pixel represents a bit. a white pixel represents one, and a black pixel represents zero.
- the bits are arranged in rows, and the bytes are arranged in columns
as well as the display of program memory, core allows for its manipulation. if core shows you a picture of a program’s insides, then it is only natural that it allows you to scribble on it. the overcommitted empty space below the stack stack provides an inviting empty space to scribble in. it’s a perfect place to hide your terrible secrets in some poor, innocent process.

core is the logical conclusion of blinkenlights, “Allblinkenlights,” if you will. the intended experience is evocative aimlessness. the human visual system is highly parallel and very good at recognizing patterns. you are encouraged to allow these patterns to wash over you.

many textures arise from different kinds of data in memory. ASCII text is incredibly recognizable, by virtue of being a 7-bit encoding, as well as having a biased distribution of values. 64-bit pointers are similarly easy to recognize because their last two bytes will either be zero or one.

in the mesmerizing undulations of complex programs, these textures may blink or move around or stay boringly still. if you are keen, you may catch some large data structure being allocated or filled in. or you may see the first generation of a garbage collector fly by as short-lived objects are created at a rapid rate. in games, the stack can be seen flickering rapidly and changing every frame.

core can make stark the immensity of memory and the way that programs use it. data structures and programming patterns appear in the physical reality of which bits are toggled where.

I was very keen to see what a program would look like that uses continuation passing style implemented as in the famous paper, CONS should not CONS its arguments, part II: Cheney on the M.T.A . I compiled a game programmed in CHICKEN scheme and was delighted to see a stack that moved like a waterfall.

graphical programs can be the most interesting. visual patterns in graphics in memory can emerge vividly.

when attached to virtual machines or emulators, core gains omniscience over an entire operating system.

it is astounding to see an immense creature flicker to life. pages fill empty space in speckled patterns. panning over a chasm, the page tables can be seen vibrating and filling in with new allocations. it is reminiscent, perhaps, of insects, like a beehive.

one could not hope to wholly understand the way that physical memory is arranged, but they may peer voyeuristically into random pages of process memory, abound with text strings and recognizable graphics.

programs often exist in the mind as something ineffable, intangible, and abstract. even their physical existence is locked inside black plastic squares, harboring impossibly tiny transistors. in my opinion, to lay visceral the individual bits in a computer program is an idea that despite being simple, is immensely potent.

peer into the core.

items.body:
# The sleep framework: A new way for LLMs to retain knowledge in continual learning

The sleep framework: A new way for LLMs to retain knowledge in continual learning October 27, 2026

Ali Behrouz and Vahab Mirrokni, Google Research

We introduce a sleep phase in continual learning, enabling large language models to continuously integrate new facts and enhance reasoning while mitigating catastrophic forgetting or static knowledge cutoffs.

Modern LLMs achieve impressive performance via pre-training and in-context learning (ICL). However, once deployed, they remain largely static, operating with a fixed knowledge cutoff date that leaves them unable to acquire long-term capabilities or adapt to new information.

While updating models with new data seems like the obvious solution, continual parameter updates often trigger catastrophic forgetting , a fundamental issue where learning new tasks severely degrades performance on previously learned ones. Alternatively, relying strictly on ICL limits knowledge retention to the immediate context window: once the context session ends, the acquired short-term information is forgotten.

Inspired by how the human brain processes and stabilizes memory during rest, we introduce a sleep framework in continual learning: a learning paradigm that equips large language models (LLMs) with a continuous periodic lifecycle, enabling them to continually learn, consolidate fragile short-term context into stable long-term parameters. With this framework, we demonstrate that alternating between active interaction and offline memory consolidation allows LLMs to continuously acquire new facts, retain long-context knowledge up to 10M tokens, and improve complex reasoning.

## Rethinking machine learning: Active (wake) vs. sleep phases

Traditional machine learning relies on a strict separation between training and inference. In a continual learning framework, this distinction becomes artificial; an intelligent agent must constantly learn, adapt, and process information.

Under the sleep paradigm, an LLM operates across two primary states:

- Active (wake) phase : The model actively receives, processes, and interacts with inputs, storing temporary information in fast, short-term memory components.
- Sleep phase : The model pauses processing new inputs and redirects its internal computations toward memory consolidation and self-improvement.
While terms like "sleep," "dreaming," and "self-improvement" borrow from neuroscience, our framework operates entirely within a fixed model architecture and human-defined training rules. During the offline sleep phase, the model unlocks pre-allocated Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) memory blocks and updates its numerical weights using self-generated practice examples. This automated post-training cycle helps a deployed model absorb new facts and sharpen its reasoning accuracy while keeping its core codebase and design unchanged.

## Key components of the sleep process

The sleep paradigm addresses catastrophic forgetting and continuous adaptation through two stages: memory consolidation and dreaming.

### 1. Memory consolidation

In the human brain, non-rapid eye movement (NREM) slow-wave sleep consolidates fragile memories into long-term structures via abstraction and distillation. Our proposed sleep framework mirrors this natural phenomenon through two key technical mechanisms:

- Parameter expansion & continuum memory hierarchy: To prevent catastrophic forgetting, the model dynamically scales its capacity during sleep. Using a Mixture of Experts (MoE) and Hope architecture , newly unlocked, low-rank experts are integrated into stable, lower-frequency memory blocks to store incoming knowledge without disrupting older parameters.
- Knowledge seeding (upward distillation): Fragile short-term memories stored in high-frequency layers (e.g., in-context memory) are transferred into the newly expanded long-term parameters. This is achieved through Generalized Knowledge Distillation (GKD) combined with reinforcement learning (RL)-based imitation learning : On-policy distillation: The expanded student model learns token-specific feedback from teacher distributions generated on self-sampled sequences.
- Learning to imitate (LTI): The student model is rewarded based on semantic and absolute similarity ( Levenshtein distance ) when completing prefixes of teacher-generated text.
- Synaptic pruning: Once the memory consolidation into lower-frequency modules is complete, the high-frequency temporary parameters are reset, freeing up capacity for future active sessions.
Overview of our sleep framework: Input streams from the active phase are stored in short-term memory before entering the sleep cycle, which bifurcates into Consolidation (transferring fragile short-term tokens into expanded long-term parametric memory using low-rank structures and MoE) and Dreaming (autonomous self-improvement via synthetic routing with random experts and RL refinement).

### 2. Dreaming for self-improvement

During REM sleep , the human brain actively simulates scenarios, consolidates emotional/semantic connections, and explores novel neural pathways. Mirroring this, during the “dreaming stage”, the sleep framework implements an autonomous self-improvement loop:

- Random expert selection: During synthetic data generation, the MoE router randomly activates non-standard experts. This forces the model to mix disparate domains of knowledge and uncover latent patterns.
- Curated rehearsal: The model generates synthetic training samples ("dreams") and filters them using gradient-based data selection to prioritize samples with the highest potential to boost overall model capability.
- RL refinement: The model performs supervised fine-tuning on top-rated dream samples and evaluates whether the generation improves performance on downstream tasks.
## Theoretical foundations

Beyond the empirical results, our sleep paradigm is grounded in a theory that clarifies why its two stages (memory consolidation and dreaming) can support continual learning without simply trading new knowledge for old capabilities.

For memory consolidation, the analysis shows that knowledge seeding can be understood as a structured, low-rank compression problem. The model is not asked to copy every detail of its short-term traces into its parameters. Instead, it identifies a compact set of directions that best preserve both the model’s own on-policy behavior and the semantic qualities rewarded by the learning objective.

# PrismML’s Bonsai 2.5 brings better coding and tool use to on-device AI - 9to5Mac

- Mac

## PrismML’s Bonsai 2.5 brings better coding and tool use to on-device AI

Back in July, PrismML claimed its roughly 4 GB, 1-bit Bonsai 27B was the first AI model of its size to run on an iPhone. Now PrismML has released Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B, an update to the model it introduced in September.

The startup also drew attention when CEO Babak Hassibi told CNBC that Apple was evaluating its technology, as we reported at the time .

The new model is based on Qwen3.8 27B and keeps the same 5.9 GB footprint in its most compact format. This time, PrismML focused on helping the model handle longer tasks, including figuring out what to do when a tool returns an unexpected result or a step fails.

Bonsai 2.5 improved on six of the seven benchmarks PrismML highlights . Its SWE-bench Verified coding score rose from 60.8 to 75.6, while its AppWorld tool-use score jumped from 51.2 to 90.5. LiveCodeBench v6 dipped from 83.8 to 83.0.

What could that look like on a Mac? A coding assistant could inspect a private project, make a change, run the tests, and use the results to revise its fix. A document app could summarize a folder of sensitive files while keeping the processing on the device.

PrismML says Bonsai 2.5 runs on Mac, iPhone, and iPad through MLX. Its Apple silicon package is about 8.9 GB, and the model card walks through setup on a Mac . The weights are available for free under Apache 2.0.

For a closer look at how the model was compressed and tested, read PrismML’s technical white paper .

items.body:
Apple experimentiert offenbar schon länger mit macOS auf dem iPad. Das bedeutet allerdings nicht, dass das Unternehmen eine Zusammenführung von iPadOS und macOS vorbereitet oder macOS künftig regulär auf seinen Tablets anbieten möchte. Vielmehr geht es um interne Entwicklungs- und Testumgebungen.

Die Möglichkeit, macOS auf iPad-Hardware auszuführen, ist vor allem für Apples Entwicklungsabteilungen interessant. So lassen sich bestimmte Funktionen und Softwarekomponenten unter realen Hardwarebedingungen testen, ohne dafür zwingend einen klassischen Mac verwenden zu müssen. Die iPad-Hardware (M-Prozessoren) dürfte in jedem Fall leistungsstark für macOS sein.

## iPadOS und macOS sollen eigenständig bleiben

Apple verfolgt weiterhin die Strategie, iPad und Mac als eigenständige Produktplattformen zu behandeln. Zwar haben sich beide Betriebssysteme in den vergangenen Jahren funktional angenähert. Funktionen wie Multitasking, Fensterverwaltung und eine umfangreichere Bedienung mit Tastatur und Maus machen das iPad zunehmend computerähnlich. Eine vollständige Übernahme von macOS ist damit aber nicht verbunden.

Auch Apples CEO John Ternus hatte sich Anfang November zur möglichen Zusammenführung der Betriebssysteme geäußert. Auf die Frage, ob Apple langfristig ein gemeinsames System für Mac und iPad plane, erklärte er, dass derzeit keine grundlegenden Änderungen in diese Richtung vorgesehen seien.

**Kein macOS für das iPad in Sicht**

Für Nutzer bedeutet das zunächst keine Veränderung. iPads werden weiterhin mit iPadOS ausgeliefert, während macOS den Macs vorbehalten bleibt. Apple kann zwar Funktionen und technische Grundlagen zwischen den Plattformen austauschen, möchte aber offenbar die unterschiedlichen Bedienkonzepte erhalten. Beim neuen MacBook Pro mit PROLED XDR Display verfolgt Apple den Ansatz, dass Tastatur und Trackpad die primären Eingabegeräte sind, während die Touch-Bedienung das Ganze ergänzt.

(via [Mark Gurman](https://omny.fm/shows/power-on-with-mark-gurman/mailbag-mark-answers-your-questions-about-apple-s-product-political-future))

items.body:
Signal announced an update to its mobile apps on iOS and Android that seeks to curb issues with AI agents accessing private chats. This is a useful new barrier against a problem we’ve been highlighting this year in our Encrypt It Already campaign. And good news, it’s enabled by default so you don’t need to do anything except update the app.

Over the last year, both Google and Apple* have released AI features in their operating systems that can read the contents of apps. One of the ways it can do this is through screen analysis. Google calls this feature “Intelligent Screen Context,” while Apple refers to it as either “Onscreen Awareness” or “Visual Intelligence.”

Apple now provides a way to block Siri AI’s access to apps, but by default every app is available to Siri AI, so it’s up to the user to go in and put these guardrails up. Signal requests that protection on your behalf. Google doesn’t currently offer any sort of similar option. So Signal on Android does the best it can, by turning off screenshots when it detects an AI assistant attempting to access the screen. Signal’s solution helps ensure that, unless you go in and change the setting yourself, it defaults to the most private option.

While this is a clever solution to the current issues facing Signal (and potentially useful for any other app that does its best to promise privacy), we need all operating systems to provide stronger methods and clear documentation to developers so they can safeguard their users without needing to jump through hoops. Both developers and users should have the tools they need to safeguard their own data from AI agents and other AI tools.

*Apple is an EFF donor. EFF donors do not influence our agenda or our positions.

items.body:
After backlash from sellers frustrated by Etsy’s new AI policies, which appeared to allow the company to train AI on user artwork, Etsy has now clarified its stance.

In a note [published](https://www.etsy.com/news/etsyas-terms-of-use?ref=news) on Monday, CEO Kruti Patel Goyal discussed recent tweaks to the company's terms of service and admitted that her team "should’ve given you more context on what the updates meant for your creative content."

“Our recent terms update was meant to reflect the evolving technologies we're using to build better tools and experiences for sellers and the Etsy community,” Goyal wrote this week. “It was not meant to enable us to train AI models for the purpose of creating copycats of your items. We do not and will not do that.”

## Der erste Eindruck zum Sterling StingRay 50th Anniversary LTD

Schick, schick, der Herr! Die sind ja mal richtig gut gelungen, will ich bereits vorwegnehmen. Die neuen StingRay-Bässe zum 50. Jubiläum können optisch sofort überzeugen. Aus Erfahrung wissen wir, dass die Sterling-Instrumente wirklich sehr gute Alternativen zu den, weitaus teureren Music-Man-Modellen aus den USA sind. Schauen wir uns die Zutaten für die neue Serie genauer an

Sterling StingRay 50th Anniversary LTD · Quelle: Sterling

## Die Zutaten im Detail

Der Sterling StingRay 50th Anniversary LTD besitzt einen Korpus aus Okumé. Der Hals ist aus wunderschön geröstetem Ahorn gefertigt und hat ein Griffbrett aus Palisander obendrauf. Dieses ist mit großen, weißen Pearloid-Block-Griffbretteinlagen geschmückt. Die Hardware ist komplett in Gold gehalten und besteht aus einem klassischen, von Sterling entworfenen Steg und offenen Mechaniken. Das macht auf dem Papier zunächst einmal einen sehr soliden Eindruck.

Sterling StingRay 50th Anniversary LTD · Quelle: Sterling

## Aktiver Tonabnehmer

Besonders hervorzuheben ist der **aktive Alnico-Humbucker**, der über ein**3-Band-Preamp** geregelt wird. Damit lässt sich, wie vom StingRay bekannt, klanglich enorm viel abdecken. Stilistisch seid ihr mit dem Bass niemals in einem Korsett gefangen. Das Batteriefach für den Preamp ist dezent über die Rückseite des Korpus zugänglich.

Sterling Alnico-Humbucker · Quelle: Sterling

items.body:
# USA: US-Gericht spricht Huawei wegen Betrugs schuldig

Huawei: Der chinesische Technologiekonzern wurde vor Gericht schuldig gesprochen. Foto: IMAGO/ZUMA Wire New York. Der chinesische Technologiekonzern Huawei ist in den USA in einem jahrelangen Strafverfahren schuldig gesprochen worden. Eine Jury in Brooklyn befand das Unternehmen am Dienstag in zehn von zwölf Anklagepunkten für schuldig, darunter Bankbetrug, Verstöße gegen Sanktionen und Diebstahl von Geschäftsgeheimnissen.

Die Vorwürfe entbehrten jeder rechtlichen Grundlage, teilte Huawei mit. Man werde rechtliche Schritte einleiten, um die eigenen Rechte zu schützen. Vom Vorwurf der Bildung einer kriminellen Vereinigung sprachen die Geschworenen den Netzwerkausrüster frei.

Die Anklage warf Huawei vor, Banken wie HSBC über Geschäfte im Iran getäuscht zu haben. Meldungen der Nachrichtenagentur Reuters aus den Jahren 2012 und 2013 hatten maßgeblich dazu beigetragen, diese Aktivitäten aufzudecken. Den Geschworenen lag zudem eine Erklärung der Huawei-Finanzchefin Meng Wanzhou vor, in der sie illegale Iran-Geschäfte eingeräumt hatte.

Das Gericht sah es ferner als erwiesen an, dass Huawei über zwei Jahrzehnte hinweg Technologien von US-Firmen wie Cisco und T-Mobile gestohlen hat. Die Verteidigung wies dies zurück: Die Anklage habe sich lediglich unzusammenhängende Vorfälle herausgepickt. Der Erfolg von Huawei beruhe auf eigener Forschung.

items.body:
In [an announcement on Wednesday](https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/DOC-427572A1.pdf), the FCC says it authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million AI chip-equipped satellites as part of the Elon Musk-owned [company's "Starmind" initiative](https://www.spacex.com/spacexsi/starmind). With [several others also pursuing the idea of putting AI data centers in space](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/845453/space-data-centers-astronomers), including Google and Blue Origin, this is the first approval the agency has granted for a full "constellation" of AI satellites.

[The FCC's approval requires](https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/DA-26-1273A1.pdf) SpaceX to deploy at least one satellite by 2033, and meet the 1 million satellite milestone by 2040. The FCC also deferred SpaceX's request to dispose of satellites located above 600km in [space "graveyard" orbits](https://www.nesdis.noaa.gov/news/graveyard-orbits-and-the-satellite-afterlife), rather than …

[Read the full story at The Verge.](https://www.theverge.com/science/1042278/spacex-fcc-starmind-ai-space-data-centers)

items.body:
For the first time ever, a foreign astronaut has set foot inside China's Tiangong space station.

That pioneer is Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, who arrived at [Tiangong](https://www.space.com/tiangong-space-station) aboard the [Shenzhou-24](https://www.space.com/space-exploration/human-spaceflight/china-rolls-out-rocket-for-launch-of-1st-international-astronaut-to-tiangong-space-station-video) spacecraft early this morning (Nov. 25).

"The Chinese space station is always something to look forward to!" the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) wrote in [an update today](https://www.cmse.gov.cn/xwzx/202611/t20261125_57903.html) (in Mandarin; translation by Google). "China's 'Tiangong' welcomes partners from all over the world to visit!"

Ali, a former pilot in Pakistan's armed forces, is a payload specialist on Shenzhou-24. He found his way onto the mission thanks to a space-cooperation agreement that China signed with Pakistan in Islamabad [in February 2025](https://www.space.com/space-exploration/human-spaceflight/china-and-pakistan-agree-to-fly-1st-foreign-astronaut-to-chinese-space-station).

Ali and his two Shenzhou-24 crewmates — commander Tang Hongbo and flight engineer Wu Yi — enjoyed a short and smooth ride to their orbital destination. They [lifted off](https://www.space.com/space-exploration/human-spaceflight/china-shenzhou-24-first-international-astronaut-launch-tiangong-space-station) atop a Long March 2F rocket on Tuesday (Nov. 24) at 7:18 p.m. EST (0018 GMT on Nov. 25) and reached Tiangong a little over six hours later.

Tang and Wu will live aboard the outpost for the usual six-month stint. Ali, however, will come home in just a week, hitching a ride with two of the three Shenzhou-23 astronauts, who [arrived at Tiangong in May](https://www.space.com/space-exploration/human-spaceflight/china-shenzhou-23-astronaut-launch-tiangong-space-station).

Ali will be busy during his short space stay, conducting a set of joint Chinese-Pakistani experiments.

"Four collaborative projects in biotechnology and materials are planned, with Ali also scheduled to conduct an in-orbit experiment involving photosynthetic cyanobacteria," The Times of India [wrote today](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/science/pak-astronaut-ali-reaches-chinas-tiangong-station/articleshow/136152904.cms).

The third Shenzhou-23 crewmate, Zhu Yangzhu, will remain on the station until Shenzhou-24 comes home. Zhu will therefore set a Chinese record, becoming the first astronaut from his country to live in [low Earth orbit](https://www.space.com/low-earth-orbit) for a full year.

Astronauts from the Soviet Union/Russia and the United States have already blazed this long-duration trail. The global record for longest continuous space stay is 437 days, set by cosmonaut Valeri Polyakov aboard the [Mir space station](https://www.space.com/31999-mir-space-station-30th-anniversary.html) from January 1994 to March 1995.

Another look at the Shenzhou-23 and Shenzhou-24 astronauts aboard Tiangong on Nov. 25, 2026. (Image credit: CMSA)

Ali is not the first person from Pakistan ever to reach space, by the way. That distinction belongs to adventurer Namira Salim, who [traveled to suborbital space](https://www.space.com/virgin-galactic-first-pakistani-space-galactic04) on a tourism flight with [Virgin Galactic](https://www.space.com/18993-virgin-galactic.html) in October 2023.

Shenzhou-24 is the 12th crewed mission to Tiangong, a three-module, T-shaped outpost that China finished assembling in late 2022. Well, "finished" might not be the right term; China [plans to expand Tiangong](https://www.space.com/space-exploration/launches-spacecraft/china-plans-to-double-the-size-of-its-tiangong-space-station-while-the-iss-nears-its-end), which is currently about 20% as massive as the [International Space Station](https://www.space.com/space-exploration/missions/international-space-station).

items.body:
Josie Ford

**[Feedback](https://www.newscientist.com/topic/feedback)** is our weekly column of bizarre stories, implausible advertising claims, confusing instructions and more

Reader Jenny Ozanne writes to tell us of a horrific incident that befell her partner. He had bought [Audrey Niffenegger’s novel](https://www.newscientist.com/article/2594474-theres-two-ways-of-doing-time-travel-right-says-audrey-niffenegger/) *The Time Traveler’s Wife* as a CD audiobook, to listen to on long car journeys.

“After a while, he complained that the plot was completely impossible to follow,” writes Jenny. “It was only when I checked his player that I realized he had accidentally set the CD to ‘shuffle’. “

Jenny raises two points, which Feedback heartily endorses: “I’m still not sure what’s more impressive: the story’s ability to survive total chronological chaos, or the fact that he listened to three random chapters before suspecting anything was wrong.”

Feedback would suggest that *The Time Traveler’s Wife* might be the ideal novel to experience on shuffle, since the narrative is heavily non-linear. The main character hops uncontrollably back and forth through history. This led us to wonder: would any similarly chrono-displaced stories survive the experience of being played on shuffle, or even be improved by it?

We wondered, for instance, about David Mitchell’s *Cloud Atlas*. This has six stories set in different periods, including a future in which human clones are used as cheap labour, and a more distant future in which everything has gone a bit *Mad Max*. The stories are linked by characters in later timelines reading about the earlier ones, and by subtle coincidences. What would it be like on shuffle?

However, after careful reflection, we realised there is only one correct answer to this, and that is Shane Carruth’s 2004 film *Primer*, which tells the story of two tech bros who invent a time machine in their garage. At first, they use it to go back in time and make money on the stock exchange, only to become caught up in an escalating web of betrayal and deception as they endlessly rewrite their lives.

*Primer* is so overcomplicated, so mind-wreckingly confusing, that some poor soul once went so far as to draw a diagram trying to convey its timeline. [Posted on Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/r/movies/comments/1wxpfc/detailed_explanationtimeline_of_shane_carruths/) by u/Clawz114, the diagram looks like a cross between a metro map and a flowchart of the inner workings of a chemical factory. It is therefore possible that playing the scenes in random order might actually cause the film to make more sense.

## The scent of success

It’s that time of year when many of us are thinking, “Oh blimey, I need to buy everyone presents” and then having a meltdown when we can’t think of anything. The last refuge of the true gift scoundrel is, of course, the scented candle. This item might as well come with a note saying, “Sorry, I couldn’t think of anything”.

Readers looking to step up their scented candle game may wish to investigate [JD + Kate Industries](https://jdandkateindustries.com/), which is run by a pair of humour writers with a sideline in themed scented candles. They have taken these tedious items to new and different places.

For instance, consider the Late Bronze Age Collapse scented candle, which “commemorates everyone’s favorite late 13th century [BC] widespread societal collapse”. Happily, it doesn’t smell of violence and decay, but rather of “burning cedar”, since “Lebanese cedar was a popular building material in the Late Bronze Age”.

Those with more contemporary tastes may wish to consider the AI scented candle, which has a little sculpture of a data centre on the top, “surrounded by a post-apocalyptic, bombed-out city”. What does it smell of, you ask? “Diesel generator exhaust fumes”.

Finally, those nostalgic for the headier days of space exploration might appreciate the Apollo 11 scented candle. Disappointingly, this doesn’t smell of moon dust, which, as we understand it, basically smells of burning because it reacts with oxygen on contact. Instead, its scent mimics “a certain powdered orange drink mix often associated with the space program, but that was not brought on Apollo 11. The astronauts brought a generic, grapefruit-flavored powdered drink mix instead, because they selfishly did not consider us and our desire to market candles.”

Feedback has no idea if these candles are any good, but we enjoyed JD + Kate’s website a lot.

## By the letter

Let us foray once again into the wonderful world of scientific acronyms. First, two reader claims that, for reasons that will become obvious, we cannot verify.

Michael Berkson tells us: “As a solicitor my late wife was involved in development of insurance for doctors. The firm had to tell the client that they needed to choose a better name. Their original choice was Professional Indemnity Support Scheme.” Michael says the clients were open to replacing “scheme” with “service”, which helps not at all.

Likewise, Jim Taylor asserts that he was once confronted with a military programme intended to ensure that spare parts would always be available for key equipment. It was called the Contractor Repair Advanced Provisioning System.

Finally, a story we can confirm is true because we looked it up. Reader Geraldine Beare is an indexer, which is one of those jobs that we often forget about but would swiftly notice if it wasn’t done. “I am at present indexing a book on goats,” says Geraldine. Through this assignment she has learned the acronym “OMAGOD”, which she recommends saying “quickly, or perhaps in a vaguely Scottish accent”. It actually stands for ovine mouth and gum obscure disease.

**Got a story for Feedback?**

*You can send stories to Feedback by email at feedback@newscientist.com. Please include your home address. This week’s and past Feedbacks can be [seen on our website](https://www.newscientist.com/article-type/feedback/).*

items.body:
WhatsApp arbeitet an einer neuen Möglichkeit, Unterhaltungen etwas lebendiger zu gestalten. Künftig lassen sich animierte Sticker mit Ton versehen und direkt innerhalb eines Chats abspielen. Die Funktion wird bereits an erste Nutzer der iPhone-Beta verteilt. Gleichzeitig erweitert die Tagesschau ihr Angebot innerhalb des Messengers um einen eigenen Kanal für Nachrichten in Einfacher Sprache.

## Eigene Sticker mit Ton erstellen

Wie [WABetaInfo berichtet](https://wabetainfo.com/whatsapp-is-rolling-out-sticker-messages-with-audio-on-ios/), unterstützt die aktuelle WhatsApp-Testversion 26.46.10.70 für iOS sogenannte Sound-Sticker. Dabei handelt es sich um animierte Sticker, die zusätzlich eine kurze Tonspur enthalten.

Eigene Sound-Sticker lassen sich direkt im Sticker-Editor erstellen. Dazu wird zunächst ein Video aus der Fotomediathek ausgewählt, das WhatsApp automatisch in einen animierten Sticker umwandelt. Über eine neue Schaltfläche kann anschließend ein passender Ton hinzugefügt werden.

Zur Auswahl stehen der Originalton des Videos, verschiedene vorgefertigte Geräusche sowie eigene Aufnahmen. Auch Audiodateien aus der Dateien-App lassen sich verwenden. Wer möchte, kann direkt im Editor eine kurze Sprachnachricht aufnehmen.

## Wiedergabe erst nach Antippen

Damit Gruppenchats nicht plötzlich zur Geräuschkulisse werden, spielen die Sticker ihren Ton nicht automatisch ab. Stattdessen erscheint ein kleines Lautsprechersymbol, über das die Wiedergabe gestartet werden kann. Der Ton wird anschließend dreimal wiederholt.

Die Neuerung ist zunächst für ausgewählte Betatester verfügbar. Vereinzelt soll sie bereits in der regulären App-Store-Version auftauchen. Wann WhatsApp die Funktion für alle Nutzer freischaltet, ist noch offen. Schon bisher konnten Anwender [eigene Sticker aus Fotos erstellen](https://www.iphone-ticker.de/whatsapp-schaltet-neue-formatier-optionen-fuer-alle-nutzer-frei-230439/).

## Tagesschau startet Kanal in Einfacher Sprache

Abseits der neuen Sticker gibt es auch Neuigkeiten bei den WhatsApp-Kanälen. Die ARD bietet ihre „Tagesschau in Einfacher Sprache“ ab sofort über einen [eigenen WhatsApp-Kanal](https://www.tagesschau.de/ard-angebote-in-leichter-und-einfacher-sprache) an. Damit erweitert der Sender sein seit 2024 bestehendes Nachrichtenangebot.

Von Montag bis Freitag veröffentlicht die Redaktion von ARD-aktuell dort Texte zu ausgewählten Nachrichten sowie einen Link zur vollständigen Sendung. Regelmäßig wird außerdem auf weitere Nachrichtenangebote in Leichter und Einfacher Sprache hingewiesen.

Das Format richtet sich unter anderem an Menschen mit Schwierigkeiten beim Lesen oder Lernen, Menschen mit kognitiven Einschränkungen sowie Personen, die Deutsch lernen. Kurze Sätze und verständliche Begriffe sollen den Zugang zu aktuellen Nachrichten erleichtern.

Parallel hat die ARD eine neue Übersichtsseite eingerichtet, auf der sämtliche entsprechenden Nachrichtenangebote gebündelt werden. Wer dem neuen Kanal folgt und die Glocke aktiviert, kann sich über neue Beiträge benachrichtigen lassen.

[★ iPhone-Ticker bei Google bevorzugen ★](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=iphone-ticker.de)

Der Beitrag [WhatsApp: Sticker bekommen Ton, Tagesschau startet neuen Kanal](https://www.iphone-ticker.de/whatsapp-sticker-bekommen-ton-tagesschau-startet-neuen-kanal-291402/) Wurde zuerst auf [iphone-ticker.de](https://www.iphone-ticker.de) veröffentlicht.

items.title: Ninajirachi’s studio gear, from Ableton stock plugins to iPhone voice memos
items.subtitle: Ninajirachi is still riding her meteoric ascension into superstardom.
items.feedText: The Australian-born producer just won another ARIA Award for Best Dance/Electronic Release for WannaCry, her collaboration with Porter Robinson (who just so happens to be one of her personal heroes). She won three last year for her debut album, I Love My Computer, followed by a performance at Coachella, which was brimming with her self-described “girl EDM” sound. She’s also slated for a massive closing set at Primavera Sound 2027, playing back-to-back with Skrillex, and just released the remix album of her debut…
items.body:
[Ninajirachi](https://musictech.com/artists/ninajirachi/) is still riding her meteoric ascension into superstardom. The Australian-born producer just won another ARIA Award for Best Dance/Electronic Release for *WannaCry*, her collaboration with [Porter Robinson](https://musictech.com/artists/porter-robinson/) (who just so happens to be one of her personal heroes). She won three last year for her debut album, *I Love My Computer*, followed by a performance at [Coachella](https://musictech.com/brands/coachella/), which was brimming with her self-described “girl EDM” sound. She’s also slated for a massive closing set at [Primavera Sound](https://musictech.com/brands/primavera-sound/) 2027, playing back-to-back with [Skrillex](https://musictech.com/artists/skrillex/), and just released the remix album of her debut, titled *I Love My Computer, All My Friends Are Inside It.*

*MusicTech* has hosted Ninajirachi many times along this epic journey. She was [a cover star in 2024](https://musictech.com/features/interviews/ninajirachi-interview-girl-edm-disc-1/), and she was [on our My Forever Studio podcast in 2025](https://musictech.com/shows/podcasts/my-forever-studio/my-forever-studio-ninajirachis-endearing-soft-synth-selection/). In these chats, she went deep into her philosophy and process behind her bombastic, computerised beats that harken back to the global EDM movement.

Below are some of her favourite pieces of gear that she’s used along her upward journey.

## Ableton Live

Nina made the shift from [FL Studio](https://musictech.com/tag/image-line-fl-studio/) to [Ableton Live](https://musictech.com/tag/ableton-live/) in 2018, with the [DAW](https://musictech.com/tag/daws/) and its tools becoming a key driver of her definitive girl EDM sound.

Having started with only her laptop, she developed a natural workflow in Live, leaning on some of its stock plugins such as Wavetable, Operator, and Simpler. She’s specifically cited Wavetable as her go-to for making Reese basses.

“I feel like it’s everything I need and nothing I don’t for a simple sound design moment,” Nina told *MusicTech* in her cover feature. “I think because of the way I learned to use Ableton really methodically when I was 18 or so, it just stuck with me. I can navigate and edit so fast. The most streamlined process from brain to page is always what I’m looking for, and Ableton has done that for me.”

[deals ids=”411f0e62-a32f-4217-b258-3ceb2f6338cf”]

## Genelec 8330A Studio Monitors

Despite only needing a DAW and a laptop to design award-winning sounds, Nina invested in a pair of [Genelec](https://musictech.com/brands/genelec/) 8330A [monitors](https://musictech.com/tag/monitors/). She previously produced music using her [Apple](https://musictech.com/brands/apple/) wired EarPods, but as she began to progress in her career, she realised how much difference a reliable pair of speakers can make.

“I think they really have improved my work a lot. I can just hear everything really well on them,” Nina says, speaking of the Genelec 8330A’s. When it came to picking from the vast array of [studio](https://musictech.com/tag/studios/) monitors available, she cites a friend/professional [mixing](https://musictech.com/tag/mixing/) and [mastering](https://musictech.com/tag/mastering/) engineer in her *My Forever Studio* interview who was dedicated to the Genelec brand.

“He was all about Genelec and his room sounded so amazing. I started to get better at mixing my own music just by virtue of working in his room.”

## Bluebird SL Mic

An essential element of Nina’s girl EDM sound is her own [vocals](https://musictech.com/tag/vocals/) that she’s delivered on tracks such as *Sing Good*, *Cut the Rope*, and *Fuck My Computer*. She has several mics she uses for [recording](https://musictech.com/tag/recording/) vocals, but her favourite is the lesser-known [Blue](https://musictech.com/brands/blue-microphones/) Bluebird SL XLR Cardioid Condenser [Microphone](https://musictech.com/tag/microphones/).

The mic is surprisingly affordable, packs a vintage-inspired chassis, and is primed for vocals, acoustic instruments, and podcasts recordings. It also has a high-pass filter and -20dB pad to customise it to your recording source.

“I’ve got a few different little mics at home, but the one I probably like the most is the blue Bluebird mic. It’s nice and crisp, and I like how it makes me sound…My favourite colour is blue, so it’s nice to look at,” Nina told us on *My Forever Studio.*

## FabFilter Pro-L 2

[FabFilter](https://musictech.com/brands/fabfilter/)’s celebrated limiter plugin has helped turn many a laptop into a professional mastering house, and that includes Ninajirachi. When she started touring a lot, the tracks she made in transit were not up to snuff to play out at the next gig.

“I can’t just go to studios while I’m touring all the time to fix this stuff,” Nina says. She put out a tweet explaining the issue, and her friend and fellow producer Gaszia replied recommending [FabFilter Pro-L 2](https://musictech.com/products/fabfilter-pro-l-2-limiter-plugin/). “I know the [FabFilter] bundle is super popular. I’d seen heaps of people using it, but I mostly just use native software, so I hadn’t really thought about it up until that point. But I’ve been a fan of his music for more than 10 years. Everything he releases just sounds so good all the time. I always play his music in DJ sets. So, I took his advice and bought it, and I love it.”

[deals ids=”32cc6020-1402-427a-801b-6f821ef07770″]

## Sonic Charge’s Synplant 2

Nina gave this AI-powered plugin a place in her forever studio. It was between this and [Serum 2](https://musictech.com/reviews/software-instruments/xfer-records-serum-2-review/), but she chose [Synplant 2](https://musictech.com/reviews/plug-ins/sonic-charges-synplant-2-review/) because of its penchant for creating happy accidents.

Centred around a plant graphic, the plugin lets you morph and wrangle synth sounds using 12 Branches, and planting new Seeds to manipulate. The headline feature of Synplant 2 is the Genopatch, which lets you import an audio sample, and watch the synth try to generate optimal synth settings to match the sample.

“That thing is so cool. It’s got that section where you can drop in any bit of audio, and it’ll try to recreate it,” Nina says. “It’s kind of like a sample digging machine, but then it’s a patch. So you can also do all of the standard synth stuff with it as well…The part that’s cool is when it gets it wrong. So it’s trying to recreate a kick drum, and it sounds like a fart or something, but in an interesting way.”

## An Apple iPhone

Ninajirachi. Image: Billy Zammit for MusicTech

items.body:
# Kommentar: Vanessa Emde und die Berliner Linke – dieser Ausschluss war überfällig - Meinung - SZ.de

Vanessa Emde nach der Fraktionssitzung. Christian Mang/REUTERS Es ist richtig, dass die Partei, die künftig die Regierende Bürgermeisterin stellen will, diese Abgeordnete aus ihrer Fraktion ausschließt. Zu diesem Kraftakt darf man gratulieren - und noch einen Wunsch äußern.

D ie Linkspartei im Berliner Abgeordnetenhaus hat Schluss gemacht mit Vanessa Emde. Das ist nicht schön, aber es ist richtig. Die Abgeordnete, die seit Monaten ihre Parteifreunde auf Trab hält und sich immer weiter verzettelt hat in Provokationen zum Nahost -Konflikt, ist am Dienstagabend aus der Fraktion ausgeschlossen worden. Ein Kraftakt war das für ihre Partei, vor allem aber eine Demonstration. Die Linke will Berlin regieren, zusammen mit Grünen und SPD. Wenn das überhaupt gelingen kann, dann nur auf Basis eines unmissverständlichen Signals: Mit Judenhass gezündelt wird nicht in der Stadt.

Regierungsbildung in Berlin : Ende für Emde – Linksfraktion schließt Abgeordnete aus Auf dem Weg zur ersten Linken-Bürgermeisterin in Berlin kann Elif Eralp einen wichtigen Erfolg verbuchen. Die wegen ihrer radikalen Positionen umstrittene Abgeordnete Emde fliegt aus der Fraktion.

Copilot Money’s Money Assistant, dashboard, and budget suggestions on iPhone

[Copilot Money](https://www.copilot.money/download?utm_source=macstories&utm_medium=editorial&utm_campaign=macstories_112326&utm_content=post&promo=MACSTORIES), the award-winning money tracking app that brings your spending, budgets, investments, and net worth together, has just launched its biggest feature yet: Money Assistant. It’s an AI financial agent that works across the app to spot trends, answer questions, and help you plan for the future.

Money Assistant works in the background, surfacing opportunities and suggestions proactively. It flags unexpected charges, finds refunds as they come in, and recommends budget updates as your spending changes. You can even give it standing instructions, like “Tag next week’s transactions with ‘Vacation.’” It’s a great way to manage your finances closely with less effort.

Your assistant is also available to chat. Because the Money Assistant already knows your full financial picture, you can ask “How are my stocks performing?” or “Am I on track to retire in 20 years?” and you’ll get answers that tie to your own situation.

If you’re new to Copilot Money, you’ll get personalized insights from the minute you start using the app. And, as soon as you hook up your bank accounts, the Money Assistant analyzes spending, income, and investments to build a budget based on your actual income and spending, greatly reducing the friction of getting started.

Privacy remains at the center of Copilot Money, too. Your financial data stays yours. Copilot Money doesn’t sell it or use it to train external AI models.

MacStories readers can get an extended two-month free trial with code MACSTORIES. Visit [Copilot Money](https://www.copilot.money/download?utm_source=macstories&utm_medium=editorial&utm_campaign=macstories_112326&utm_content=post&promo=MACSTORIES) to meet your Money Assistant and start your free trial today.

This offer is available to new users only. Copilot Money is available on Web, iPhone, Mac, and iPad. The Money Assistant is currently available only on iPhone, with more platforms coming next.

items.body:
Recently many people are debating whether AI will lead to our disempowerment. One simple example is that we might use AI to pursue or solve various intellectual tasks for us, rather than doing it ourselves.

So say there are twenty important math problems, and we let the AIs (with some human guidance) take a crack at them. Say the AIs solve seventeen of those problems, the humans one, and two remain unsolved.

Alternately, say we ban or limit AIs, and over a longer period of time the humans solve three of those problems. The rest go unsolved.

Arguably in the latter situation the humans are exercising more agency and, as unaided humans, achieving greater things. But in the former situation there is more discovery, possibly more usefulness, and the marginal impact of total human effort (including building the AIs) is far greater.

Which scenario involves greater “disempowerment”? I do not view the concept of disempowerment as entirely well defined, but it seems to my virgin eyes that the humans are more “disempowered” in the latter case, where only three of the problems get solved.

And take those two extra problems that get solved (eventually) by humans. Should we feel empowered if we achieve two theorem proofs due to what you might call protectionism, or how about labeling it “DEI for humans”?

Say I was working on a difficult economics problem, and I learned that an unpublished manuscript from China had solved the problem. But no one else knows about the manuscript, except for me that is. I could announce the manuscript and give it full credit. Or I could ignore the manuscript and claim the credit, and the “empowerment,” for myself. Should I feel so satisfied by that latter approach?

Or let’s say that Chinese manuscript does not exist, but I could help to create it by a well-targeted EV grant. I decline to give the grant so I can do the work myself and feel “empowered.” Am I really so empowered? Or is it a kind of phony triumph, because someone or something else could have done it better.

(One thing I have always liked about being an academic economist, or for that matter an internet writer, is knowing that I am competing against the entire world. In the U.S. academic job market there has been de facto open borders for a long time, since university employers usually will get visas for their hires, and do not shy away from doing that, even today.)

As for AI, should I feel so good and empowered if I achieve things only by deliberately holding the machines back? Or, in that scenario, am I just a loser who deliberately shuns competition?

Here is [one relevant tweet](https://x.com/centralunplan/status/2123301123901804658?a=XXtuj-4hIL366IlB0QM&s=61).

In general, I am not persuaded by the notion of empowering humans by bathing the world in protectionism and “DEI for humans.” I feel humans will be empowered best by finding their true marginally most important contributions and making those. Whether or not that involves doing the exact same things we are contributing at today.

items.body:
In a Grade 2 classroom in Rautahat, in Nepal’s southern plains, teacher Renuka Dahal holds up a picture card of a mango. She gives the Nepali word, then asks her students what they call it at home. They respond in Tharu and Maithili, the languages many of them speak with their families.

“I ask my students to teach me words in their language,” [she told UNICEF in 2025](https://www.unicef.org/nepal/stories/speaking-their-language). “It makes them feel that I care about who they are.” And that small exchange marks a real change.

For Canadians interested in Indigenous language revitalization, and for teachers welcoming newcomer students, Nepal’s experience shows what it takes to move language rights off paper and into the classroom.

For generations, many children in Nepal started school in a language they didn’t understand. Yet [research shows that beginning school in a familiar language can strengthen learning and make it easier to acquire additional languages](https://www.unesco.org/en/languages-education/need-know?hub=67098), including Nepali and English.

Nepal has written that lesson into its [2015 Constitution, which guarantees communities the right to education in their mother tongue](https://shisiradhikari.com.np/library/567/1321).

## A country of 124 mother tongues

Nepal is one of the most [linguistically diverse countries in the world](https://languageonthemove.com/counting-the-uncountable-linguistic-diversity-in-nepal/), though the state has [not always acknowledged it](https://shs.hal.science/halshs-03083343/document). The 2021 census [recorded 124 mother tongues](https://doi.org/10.3126/jns.v16i1.71780).

Fifty years earlier, in 1971, when the [Panchayat regime](https://doi.org/10.1177/002088176400600202) was promoting Nepali above all other languages, [the census counted just 17 languages](https://irjmmc.edu.np/index.php/irjmmc/article/view/265). Today, Nepali is the first language of [just under 45 per cent of the population](https://nepalitimes.com/decoding-diversity).

I have worked in Nepal since 1991, first as a volunteer schoolteacher and later as a linguist and anthropologist. I have spent decades researching [the country’s linguistic diversity](https://soscbaha.org/book-release-a-grammar-of-the-thangmi-language/). The census numbers reflect a shift I have witnessed on the ground, in communities.

In 2021, for the first time, [the census asked people about their ancestral language](https://myrepublica.nagariknetwork.com/news/use-of-nepali-language-rises-sharply-over-two-decades-69-76.html) as well as their mother tongue. [Nearly three million more people name Nepali as their mother tongue than they name it as their ancestral language](https://censusresults.nsonepal.gov.np/files/result-folder/Language%20in%20Nepal.pdf), a sign that many families have shifted to Nepali.

For other languages, the gap goes the other way. [Some 300,000 more people name Nepal Bhasa, the language of the Newar community, as their ancestral language than name it as their mother tongue](https://censusresults.nsonepal.gov.np/files/result-folder/Language%20in%20Nepal.pdf).

Nepali is also spreading as a second language: [46 per cent of the population now speaks it that way, up from 33 per cent in 2011](https://censusresults.nsonepal.gov.np/files/result-folder/Language%20in%20Nepal.pdf). Whatever pressures Nepal’s other languages face, Nepali is certainly not a language at risk.

## Rights on paper

On paper, Nepal’s laws side with children. The government’s [School Education Sector Plan 2022-32](https://www.globalpartnership.org/content/school-education-sector-plan-2022-2032-nepal) commits to scaling up early-grade teaching in children’s mother tongues.

In practice, implementation has been sluggish and uneven. [As comparative education scholar Uma Pradhan has shown](https://doi.org/10.1093/9780190685065.003.0027), policy has long treated mother tongues as a bridge to Nepali, a stepping stone to be left behind, with the state offering little support.

[In a 2026 study from Tanahun](https://doi.org/10.1080/01434632.2026.2656490), one grandparent spoke about a granddaughter in Grade 2 who was being taught only in Nepali and English: “She [does not have the] opportunity to study in [her ancestral] language; so, there is a gap.”

Grade 1 students at Shree Sahara Bal Primary School in Pokhara, Nepal, in June 2013.
[(Photo by Jim Holmes for AusAID)](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Grade1,_Shree_Sahara_Bal_Primary_School,_Pokhara,_Pokhara,_Nepal._(10699534855).jpg), [CC BY](http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)

## The evidence for local languages

[A 2024 study commissioned by UNICEF Nepal](https://www.unicef.org/nepal/reports/understanding-impact-languages-and-language-policies-childrens-learning-outcomes-nepal) examined language use in 30 schools across all seven provinces. Its conclusion was unequivocal. When children learn in their mother tongue or a familiar language, they take a more active part in lessons and do better in assessments and exams.

Many schools have rushed to switch to English-language teaching, often for financial reasons and with little teacher training. Yet [students taught in Nepali outscored their English-taught peers in Nepali, in science and even in English](https://www.unicef.org/nepal/reports/understanding-impact-languages-and-language-policies-childrens-learning-outcomes-nepal), according to the study’s analysis of school assessment results, which was limited in scale.

In Dailekh, in western Nepal, principal Sher Bahadur Rana [told UNICEF that teachers once corrected children who used their own “language or dialect.”](https://www.unicef.org/nepal/stories/speaking-their-language) After training in multilingual teaching, he said, “we learned that children learn faster and feel more confident when we teach them in the language they speak and understand best.”

## Obstacles to implementation

A recent review by education researchers Pariksha Onta and Amado Padilla, [covering 111 studies and policy documents](https://doi.org/10.3389/feduc.2026.1931390), points to a “persistent disconnect between constitutional commitments, classroom practice and targeted funding.”

Where mother tongues are taught at all, they are usually a subject rather than the language children learn in. Textbooks in children’s mother tongues remain scarce, and most of those that do exist are translations of Nepali materials with little locally relevant content. Far too few teachers who speak local languages are recruited or trained.
