Hi there,

When an AI project disappoints, the first reaction is to blame the model. Try a bigger one, tweak the prompt, add more instructions.

But most of the time the weak link is upstream: where the AI finds the information it needs. Chatbot, agent or search, it’s only as good as what it can retrieve.

That’s the job of a **vector database**, which stores your data so AI can find what’s relevant by meaning, not just keywords. AWS Marketplace put together a guide on how to choose one.

[Download the evaluation guide ›](https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/build-learn/vector-databases-for-ai)

**One building block behind three AI patterns:**

- Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines retrieve relevant context so your model responds from your data, not its training set.
- Agentic memory gives agents semantic recall across sessions instead of replaying conversation histories.
- Semantic search matches intent, not keywords.

All three depend on the same layer: **a vector database**.

[Explore what to evaluate for your use case](https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/build-learn/vector-databases-for-ai):

- Architecture diagrams: Each pattern mapped with Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
- Evaluation framework: Hybrid search, scaling, hosting trade-offs, embedding pipeline fit, and metadata filtering
- Free trials: Test vector databases in AWS Marketplace and start building

items.body:
# Hohe Spritpreise: Kaum Entlastung durch den Tankrabatt

## Hohe Spritpreise : Kaum Entlastung durch den Tankrabatt

Dem Staat entgehen durch das aktuelle Senken der Energiesteuer rund 2,5 Milliarden Euro. Im Mittel kommen davon pro Autohaushalt 13 Euro im Monat an.

24.11.2026

12:21 Uhr

teilen

Diesen Artikel teilen

Auch diese autofahrende Person wird den Tankrabatt vermutlich kaum, die hohen Spritpreise dafür um so mehr im Geldbeutel spüren Foto: Sina Schuldt/dpa

Von

Der Tankrabatt bringt kaum Entlastungen für die Menschen im Land. Dies ist das Ergebnis einer Studie, die das Institut für Makroökonomie und Konjunkturforschung (IMK) der gewerkschaftsnahen Hans-Böckler-Stiftung am Dienstag veröffentlicht hat. Demnach sparte ein Haushalt, der im Besitz eines Verbrenners ist, durch die Maßnahme im Mittel 13 Euro im Monat. Dabei profitierten einkommensstarke Haushalte am meisten.

Der Bundesregierung hat den Tankrabatt als Reaktion auf die im Zuge des Irankriegs gestiegenen Spritpreise eingeführt. In einer frühen Phase galt er zunächst von Mai bis Juni. Der jetzige Tankrabatt gilt seit Oktober bis Jahreswechsel. Durch die Absenkung der Energiesteuer auf Diesel und Benzin sollen die Preise an den Zapfsäulen 17 Cent pro Liter niedriger sein als ohne Rabatt. Die aktuelle Senkung kostet den Staat rund 2,5 Milliarden Euro.

„Der Tankrabatt hat schnell und unmittelbar die Inflationsrate gedämpft. Das war ein wichtiger Effekt“, sagt IMK-Chef Sebastian Dullien. „Er hat allerdings auch eine Reihe von Nachteilen, sodass er für eine langfristige Entlastung bei hohen Energiepreisen nicht ideal ist.“ So kam die Wirkung des Rabattes hauptsächlich bei reichen Autofahrern an. Während sich der Effekt bei Haushalten mit einem Einkommen von maximal 2.000 Euro auf im Mittel 7 Euro im Monat belief, waren es an der Spitze der Einkommensverteilung 19 Euro. Insgesamt entfielen auf das reichste Viertel rund 45 Prozent des gesamten Entlastungsvolumens.

## Ein Drittel spart woanders

Damit ist die Wirkung des Tankrabatts so gering, dass die Menschen sie gar nicht wahrnehmen. 61 Prozent der im Rahmen der IMK-Studie befragten Verbrennerfahrenden gaben an, die Entlastung kaum oder gar nicht zu spüren. Stattdessen spart rund ein Drittel der Befragten wegen der hohen Spritpreise an anderer Stelle.

„Die anhaltende Verunsicherung der Menschen aufgrund der hohen Spritpreise dürfte den privaten Konsum somit zusätzlich belasten“, so die IMK-Forscher. „Insbesondere gezielte Direktzahlungen könnten als Ergänzung zu preisdämpfenden Maßnahmen wie einer Stromsteuersenkung die Kaufkraft einkommensschwacher Haushalte stärken und dazu beitragen, Einschränkungen beim Konsum abzufedern.“

# Nvidia Is Now Too Big to Hold to Account

## Nvidia Is Now Too Big to Hold to Account

## Jensen Huang and the broader AI sector represent an enormous risk for the entire public.

Put out of mind the scenes of cheering you may have seen of Jensen Huang’s return to the headquarters of perhaps the world’s most important company, Nvidia, marking his personally triumphant comeback from being unanimously ousted by his board.

Get out of your thoughts any happy notions that you have reason to celebrate just because your money, like the money of so many millions of Americans and people well beyond the country’s borders, is tied up in the U.S. stock market, which soared at this surprising turn in the news after slumping badly in response to the scandals that had swirled around Huang.

Put out of mind the scenes of cheering you may have seen of Jensen Huang’s return to the headquarters of perhaps the world’s most important company, Nvidia, marking his personally triumphant comeback from being unanimously ousted by his board.

Get out of your thoughts any happy notions that you have reason to celebrate just because your money, like the money of so many millions of Americans and people well beyond the country’s borders, is tied up in the U.S. stock market, which soared at this surprising turn in the news after slumping badly in response to the scandals that had swirled around Huang.

What has happened in recent days, culminating in Huang’s return in the face of allegations he sustained a secret affair with a woman who was in touch with China’s spy agencies, is bad news for an economy that has grown increasingly imbalanced with the enormous growth of artificial intelligence. Far better for the U.S. economy and for everyone who has a stake in it would have been a reckoning for Nvidia that forced it to undertake the hard work of corporate reform and rebuilding trust.

Nvidia, for those who have not been paying attention, makes the most indispensable product in the world of AI: graphics processing units, a specialized type of chip, so capable and advanced that it has few real competitors, including, crucially, among well-funded Chinese companies. Nvidia, however, is much more than even this. As I have written before , it sits at the center of a highly incestuous economy of AI companies, including most of the big service providers, which it funds to keep purchasing its chips. The circular funding arrangements that Nvidia sustains with its largest customers—companies with extraordinary financial leverage and seemingly bottomless capital needs—is what keeps the AI economy’s party going. Without this, the merry-go-round of this new sector would grind to a halt and make what many thought looked like a bursting bubble in recent days seem like a minor blip.

Add to this the fact that the U.S. government and President Donald Trump have seemingly become convinced that everything and anything must be permitted with Nvidia, and with AI in general, or else China will overtake the United States in the most important technology of the near future. What this gives you is something more frightening than too big to fail: a company declared too strategically important to question or to hold to account.

The reality is that almost everything about the present picture is messed up and deeply worrisome. Let’s start with the fact that Trump, who already leads a government largely unconstrained by Congress and with wildly inflated executive powers, has taken so freely to intervening in the running of major companies. In Huang’s case, he played a central role in his reinstatement, as Monday’s news revealed.

There is nothing reassuring about this, but it gets worse. There is no reason to believe that Trump has an even remotely sophisticated grasp of the technologies at the heart of Nvidia’s business or its race against competitors. What we do know is that Trump has a weakness for very powerful and wealthy men, and Huang fits this billing. In the president’s universe, he is a winner, and Trump loves to associate himself with anyone invested with such an aura. Trump even posted an AI-generated photo of Huang intended to mirror a famous image of himself after surviving an assassination attempt, with the big difference that Huang was shown hoisting a red bra.

Trump, furthermore, is not known for a deep concern about ethics, and that is putting things gently. Where do ethics enter into this? Everywhere, from Huang’s honesty and the extent to which he was forthcoming about his affair with the suspicious Chinese national and shadowy customer, Alice Huang, as well as with at least one other woman who was his direct subordinate at Nvidia, in violation of corporate rules. Ethics are also involved in the way Huang ran his company, with a historically supine board, minimal internal controls on his behavior and oversight, and the way he promoted his family members. What matters is that nothing, inside the company or outside it, checked him. In fact, it seems likely that Trump, with his own record of serial marriages, rumored affairs, and children on the make, can relate.

But even these are mere starters. If competition with China deserves inclusion in any serious conversation about the future of AI, Trump’s treatment of Huang’s situation at Nvidia has been a running chronicle of flagrant disregard for national security. Let’s count the ways. First, when the U.S. government began to look into Alice Huang’s behavior on the suspicion that she might be a spy, it never informed Jensen Huang or gave him what would have been typical: a so-called defensive briefing so that he would know what to look out for and avoid giving away valuable trade secrets or selling his company’s most advanced chips without adequate controls preventing them from being shipped onward to China.

More broadly, historians may come to see Trump’s casual disregard for normal considerations of national security to be one of the most important and unusual hallmarks of his time in power. The examples are numerous. When shown evidence that Russia or China or some other powerful adversary is conducting secret operations against U.S. interests, Trump has often waved away concerns—in effect saying, well, we do that to them, too.

Last week offered the spectacle of Trump mugging in China with that country’s leader and Russia’s Vladimir Putin, with no hint that he had complained to them about offering targeting information to Iran that has enabled that country to attack U.S. bases in the Middle East, killing U.S. troops, as is the case with Russia, or supplying drone components to Iran, as with China. Trump went yet further, though, looking like a kid in a candy shop as he entered a room to greet an awaiting Putin and exclaiming, “He’s my friend.” Lest the message be lost on anyone, he later posted a picture of the meeting with this same message on social media.

items.title: Former Trump Administration Health Adviser Misleads About mRNA Flu Vaccine
items.subtitle: Former Health and Human Services Department adviser Calley Means has misleadingly suggested that the new mRNA influenza vaccine from Moderna isn’t…
items.feedText: Less is known about it because it is a new vaccine, but trial data suggest it works better than standard flu vaccines and does not have any serious safety risks. items.body:
Former Health and Human Services Department adviser Calley Means has misleadingly suggested that the new mRNA influenza vaccine from Moderna isn’t safe and doesn’t work well. Less is known about it because it is a new vaccine, but trial data suggest it works better than standard flu vaccines and does not have any serious safety risks.

For the first time, some Americans have the option to receive an mRNA vaccine to protect against seasonal influenza. In August, after a review that found the benefits of the vaccine outweighed the risks, the Food and Drug Administration [approved](https://www.fda.gov/vaccines-blood-biologics/vaccines/mflusiva) the shot for people ages 50 and up.

The American Academy of Family Physicians has also [endorsed](https://www.aafp.org/assets/image/upload/v1791920850/pdf_2026_through_2027_influenza_guidance.pdf) it as one of several recommended flu vaccines, including it among preferred options for those 65 years of age and older.

The new vaccine was tested in a large, randomized controlled [clinical trial](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2516491) against a standard flu vaccine. The trial included 40,703 people. The group that received the Moderna vaccine had around 27% fewer cases of lab-confirmed illness from influenza than the group that received the regular vaccine, with no apparent major safety risks.

Means, a prominent [figure](https://www.statnews.com/2024/10/07/calley-means-casey-means-conservative-voices-of-chronic-disease-crisis/) within the “Make America Healthy Again” movement and brother of [withdrawn](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cr5p4pp1407o) surgeon general [nominee](https://www.factcheck.org/2026/03/factchecking-claims-in-casey-means-surgeon-general-confirmation-hearing/) Dr. Casey Means, has distorted trial data and some circumstances surrounding the vaccine’s approval to imply in recent interviews that the vaccine is dangerous and ineffective.

Speaking on Joe Rogan’s podcast on Nov. 6 after [resigning](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/rfk-jr-adviser-calley-means-resigns-amid-growing-maha-discontent-over-lack-of-progress) from his HHS role last month, Means [said](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dMBBOawFy_4&t=5791s) the vaccine “didn’t work,” with an “almost negligible” reduction in flu, and came with “massive side effects.” When Rogan asked him what these side effects were, Means replied, “It can’t be definitively said, but there were deaths.” Means did not correct Rogan when, in following along with Means’ commentary, the podcast host said the vaccine would “kill people.”

“The FDA sent a study back on the Moderna mRNA vaccine showing that there were deaths in the study group, and showing that it had a paltry absolute benefit, and that there were severe side effects, and they asked for another study to begin,” Means also [said](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/calley-means-health-and-human-services-face-the-nation-transcript-11-08-2026/) in a Nov. 8 [interview](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Bal2ks8NN9Y&t=2237s) on CBS News’ “Face the Nation.” An advisory committee ultimately “approved a vaccine that the FDA thought was not safe and effective,” he continued.

Dr. [Anna Durbin](https://publichealth.jhu.edu/faculty/798/anna-p-durbin), director of the Center for Immunization Research at Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health, told us that Means’ statements “are not accurately reflecting the safety or efficacy of the vaccine.” Durbin is a [member](https://www.fda.gov/media/194955/download) of the FDA advisory committee that reviewed data on the vaccine and voted unanimously that the benefits outweighed the risks.

The FDA did not find that deaths in the trial were vaccine-related, as we’ll explain. The agency also found the vaccine was effective compared with a standard-dose vaccine. But because the standard vaccine already works to reduce illness from flu, the absolute difference was relatively small — even though the results showed Moderna’s vaccine was superior. In addition to providing another flu vaccine option now, having an approved mRNA flu vaccine platform [could help](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2853094) in the future if there is a flu pandemic, since mRNA vaccines can be rapidly updated.

Screenshot of Calley Means from CBS News’ “Face the Nation.”

Means’ remarks are also contradicted by reporting about the events at the FDA. In February, Dr. Vinay Prasad, then the Trump administration appointee in charge of vaccines at the FDA, initially prevented the agency from reviewing Moderna’s vaccine submission, [reportedly](https://www.statnews.com/2026/02/11/moderna-flu-vaccine-application-rejected-by-prasad-overruling-fda-staff/) over the objections of FDA staff, according to STAT. Prasad [objected](https://static.modernatx.com/pm/6cef78f8-8dad-4fc9-83d5-d2fbb7cff867/38ab7558-636c-40d1-b49a-c8f51a7afa1a/38ab7558-636c-40d1-b49a-c8f51a7afa1a_viewable_rendition__v.pdf) to the design of the primary clinical trial used to test the vaccine. The trial compared the mRNA vaccine to a standard-dose flu vaccine, and not the vaccines preferentially recommended for adults 65 and older.

The FDA, however, had previously approved Moderna’s plans, and the company was seeking an approval for people 50 years of age and older, not only those 65 and older. Prasad did [not cite](https://static.modernatx.com/pm/6cef78f8-8dad-4fc9-83d5-d2fbb7cff867/38ab7558-636c-40d1-b49a-c8f51a7afa1a/38ab7558-636c-40d1-b49a-c8f51a7afa1a_viewable_rendition__v.pdf) safety concerns when he initially rejected Moderna’s submission, and he [reversed his decision](https://www.statnews.com/2026/02/23/fda-lobbying-efforts-grow-under-trump-administration/) after complaints from Moderna and, according to reporting from [multiple](https://www.politico.com/news/2026/02/18/fda-reverses-course-on-moderna-flu-shot-bid-00785799) [news outlets](https://www.cnn.com/2026/02/19/politics/midterm-elections-trump-health-care), White House intervention. (The White House has denied being involved.)

Once review was permitted to begin, FDA staff and a committee of independent vaccine [experts](https://www.fda.gov/advisory-committees/advisory-committee-calendar/vaccines-and-related-biological-products-advisory-committee-june-18-2026-meeting-announcement) reviewed the data on Moderna’s vaccine and each [concluded](https://www.fda.gov/media/194955/download) it [supported](https://www.fda.gov/media/194140/download?attachment#page=10) the vaccine’s approval. The committee does not approve vaccines but makes recommendations that the FDA then can accept or reject.

items.body:
5 min read

## Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater)

NASA’s Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom, the first fission-powered spacecraft to travel beyond Earth orbit, cruises past Mars in this artist’s concept, demonstrating nuclear electric propulsion in deep space.

NASA completed a major review for [Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom](https://www.nasa.gov/mission/space-reactor-1-freedom/) and locked in key elements of the spacecraft, which is targeted to launch in 2028 and demonstrate nuclear electric propulsion in deep space for the first time.

Experts from across the agency, the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), and industry met at NASA’s Glenn Research Center in Cleveland for a major SR-1 mission design review in October. Several key decisions were made, propelling the mission from an early concept toward a defined spacecraft design.

“SR-1 marks a pivotal step in how we travel through the solar system,” said Steve Sinacore, SR-1 Freedom program director. “This mission will be the first freight run on the railroad of the solar system, and the decisions we’re making now are laying the tracks for every nuclear-powered spacecraft that follows.”

Planned for launch in late 2028, SR-1 will use both nuclear and solar power to deliver [SkyFall](https://science.nasa.gov/mission/skyfall/), a capsule carrying three next-generation helicopters, to Mars. Once deployed, the helicopters will study Martian geology and climate history, explore new terrain, and search for signs of subsurface ice.

As NASA prepares for more ambitious exploration missions, future spacecraft and surface operations will require significantly more power than current systems can provide, particularly in environments where sunlight is limited or unavailable. SR-1 will demonstrate how fission power can enable long-duration missions, pave the way for reliable surface power systems to support NASA’s future [Moon Base](https://www.nasa.gov/moonbase/), and enable exploration deeper into the solar system.

## Key design decisions

The SR-1 Freedom spacecraft design has evolved since NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman first introduced the concept in March at the agency’s [Ignition](https://www.nasa.gov/ignition/) event, where leadership shared plans to develop a fission-powered spacecraft in time for the next Mars launch window.

One significant change is to use a shorter boom than the one shown in early illustrations. The boom separates the reactor from the spacecraft’s main body, known as the Power and Propulsion Element. The shorter boom will reduce weight, simplify assembly, and help streamline the spacecraft’s design.

Planned for launch in late 2028, Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom will use both nuclear and solar power to deliver SkyFall to Mars. This infographic explains the components of the spacecraft.

NASA and DOE experts also determined that improvements in shielding and spacecraft design will allow the reactor to operate closer to the rest of the spacecraft. This will simplify integration while maintaining the radiation protection needed for spacecraft electronics and the SkyFall payload.

Teams are continuing to evaluate other key design features, including the number of radiator panels on SR-1, output power levels of its [nuclear power module](https://www.nasa.gov/centers-and-facilities/glenn/sr-1-freedom-advances-with-progress-on-nuclear-power-module/), and how long its reactor will operate. These decisions will help shape the final spacecraft design and ensure it meets mission objectives.

In addition, the team is modifying the spacecraft’s [Power and Propulsion Element](https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/america-underway-in-space-on-nuclear-power.pdf?emrc=6b069185e993a) by updating its communications system for the journey to Mars. SR-1 Freedom will use larger X-band antenna dishes to send data across deep space back to Earth. Further maturation of the spacecraft plans will focus on reducing risk, simplifying the design, and staying on schedule.

NASA awarded a $39.3 million contract to Johns Hopkins University’s Applied Physics Laboratory to develop the heat rejection system for the spacecraft’s nuclear power module. The system will remove excess heat generated by the spacecraft’s nuclear power system, allowing it to operate safely and efficiently. The lab is working with the company Advanced Cooling Technologies as a key strategic commercial partner for providing the critical heat pipe and composite radiator technologies that will enable the system to meet the demanding mission requirements.

Awarded under the Aerospace Research, Development, and Engineering Support II contract, the contract action ensures the Applied Physics Laboratory team will design, build, test, and evaluate the system, along with producing the hardware needed for flight. The heat rejection system is a key part of demonstrating nuclear electric propulsion in space and will help lay the groundwork and industrial production foundation for future high-power nuclear systems used in deep space exploration.

## Updated mission profile

Along with the spacecraft design, teams have defined the mission timeline and planned operations.

After launch and once the spacecraft has left Earth orbit, SR-1 Freedom will activate and gradually increase reactor power. The reactor system will operate for an initial period of time before shutting down. During this period, the spacecraft will collect and send performance data back to Earth. Solar arrays will then provide power as it cruises to Mars.

NASA’s Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom, the first fission-powered spacecraft to travel beyond Earth orbit, cruises past Mars in this artist’s concept, demonstrating nuclear electric propulsion in deep space.

After delivering SkyFall to Martian orbit, SR-1 Freedom will restart its fission reactor, collecting additional data on the spacecraft’s performance in deep space.

“By refining the design and advancing this architecture, we’re not just building a spacecraft, we’re establishing the foundation for a new era of reliable, efficient transport beyond Earth orbit,” Sinacore said. “What we learn from SR-1 Freedom will shape the future of exploration for decades to come.”

With key design decisions advancing and teams across NASA, DOE, and industry working together, SR-1 Freedom is moving toward its 2028 launch goal. The mission will demonstrate new capabilities for nuclear-powered transportation and help establish the foundation for future exploration beyond Earth.

To learn more about NASA’s efforts in nuclear power in space, visit:

[https://www.nasa.gov/space-nuclear](https://www.nasa.gov/space-nuclear)

items.body:
Does a new map show the path of potential lead fallout from the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant as a viral social media post claims? No, that's not true: The map in the post is clearly labeled as the snowfall accumulation forecast from the College of DuPage NEXLAB WOOF-NAM weather model. And what the post says is the North American Military model is really the federal government's acronym for the North American Mesoscale numerical weather prediction model.

The claim appeared in [a post](https://x.com/a_dose_of_wx/status/2125243331521515594?s=46) (archived [↗ web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20261124214535/https://x.com/a_dose_of_wx/status/2125243331521515594?s=46) ) by the @a_dose_of_wx account on X on Nov. 24, 2026. It read:

> BREAKING: NEW lead fallout map from North American Military model (NAM) as they move forward with plans to detonate 5 tons of unstable explosives at an Iowa ammunition plant.

This is what the map looked like on X at the time of writing:

*(Image source: post by @a_dose_of_wx on X.)*

The U.S. Army has scheduled a controlled detonation of 68 barrels (nearly 5 tons) of unstable lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa, on Wednesday at 9 a.m. Central time (10 a.m. Eastern time), as [Iowa Public Radio reported](https://www.iowapublicradio.org/ipr-news/2026-11-24/reynolds-iowa-lead-azide-detonation-army-ammunitions-plant-ernst-grassley-middletown) (archived [↗ web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20261124224822/https://www.iowapublicradio.org/ipr-news/2026-11-24/reynolds-iowa-lead-azide-detonation-army-ammunitions-plant-ernst-grassley-middletown) ).

The map in the post does not show "lead fallout." It is clearly labeled as "snowfall accumulation" as the image below shows (red rectangle added by Lead Stories):

*(Image source: post by @a_dose_of_wx on X.)*

The image is from the [College of DuPage NEXLAB WOOF-NAM](https://weather.cod.edu/forecast/) weather prediction model (archived [↗ web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20261116220004/https://weather.cod.edu/forecast/) ). NAM is the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration's acronym for North American Mesoscale numerical weather prediction model, not the North American Military model, as the post claims. Lead Stories was able to recreate the model map here:

*(Image source: weather.cod.edu/forecast.)*

The [U.S. Army](https://www.army.mil/article/297039) (archived [↗ web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20261124183120/https://www.army.mil/article/297039) ) published two maps on Nov. 24, 2026, on a page titled "Public Safety Advisory: Controlled, Mitigated Detonation of Unstable Lead Azide at Iowa Army Ammunition Plant." The maps did not match the map posted on X.

This is a screenshot of the first map on the page at the time of writing:

*(Image source: army.mil.)*

This is a screenshot of the second map on the page at the time of writing:

*(Image source: army.mil.)*

The [Associated Press](https://apnews.com/article/lead-azide-detonation-army-iowa-trump-83f1492cc5c3e358557f1170ea2a2d40) (archived [here)](https://web.archive.org/web/20261124225539/https://apnews.com/article/lead-azide-detonation-army-iowa-trump-83f1492cc5c3e358557f1170ea2a2d40) published a map from the U.S. Army showing the potential amount of lead dust deposited on surfaces after the explosion.

This is a screenshot of the map in the article at the time of writing:

*(Image source: Associated Press.)*

items.body:
**Fettverbrennung statt Appetitzügelung: Ein von Darmbakterien produzierter Mehrfachzucker kann bei Mäusen den Energieverbrauch erhöhen und so die Fettpolster rund um die inneren Organe verkleinern. Möglich macht dies ein Eingriff in die Kommunikation zwischen Immunsystem und Fettgewebe. Auch beim Menschen könnte ein ähnlicher Mechanismus eine Rolle spielen.**

**Durham (U.S.A.).** Nicht jedes Fettpolster ist für unsere Gesundheit gleichermaßen problematisch. Besonders bedenklich ist das sogenannte viszerale Fett, das im Bauchraum die inneren Organe umgibt und hormonell aktiv ist. Ein Überschuss dieses Gewebes ist eng mit Typ-2-Diabetes und Herz-Kreislauf-Erkrankungen verknüpft.

Auch die Darmflora beeinflusst, wie viel Energie der Körper aus der Nahrung gewinnt und als Fett speichert. Doch welche Substanzen der Mikroben an der Entstehung oder dem Abbau von viszeralem Fett beteiligt sind, ist bisher erst in Ansätzen geklärt.

### Ein Drittel weniger viszerales Fett

Forscher der Duke University um Neeraj K. Surana haben nun ein Darmbakterium genauer untersucht, das solchen Fettansammlungen entgegenwirken kann. Das Bakterium Clostridium immunis gehört zur menschlichen Darmflora und hat sich schon in früheren Tierversuchen als wirksam gegen Dickdarmentzündungen erwiesen.

Eine Woche nach der einmaligen oralen Gabe dieses Bakteriums wogen die behandelten Mäuse rund drei Prozent weniger als unbehandelte Kontrolltiere. Ihr Blut enthielt zudem rund 25 Prozent weniger Triglyceride, eine Form von Blutfetten. Zwei viszerale Fettdepots waren im Verhältnis zum Körpergewicht um etwa ein Drittel kleiner, während das Unterhautfett, das braune Fettgewebe und die fettfreie Körpermasse keine nachweisbaren Veränderungen zeigten.

Auch bei einer zwölfwöchigen fettreichen Ernährung zeigte sich ein schützender Effekt: Die Kontrolltiere legten rund die Hälfte ihres Ausgangsgewichts zu. Die wöchentlich mit Clostridium immunis behandelten Mäuse nahmen hingegen etwa 13 Prozent weniger zu als die Kontrolltiere, hatten weniger viszerales Fett und eine bessere Glukosetoleranz.

### Ein chemischer Zusatz macht den Unterschied

Interessanterweise musste sich das Bakterium dafür nicht dauerhaft im Darm ansiedeln. Schon 48 Stunden nach der Verabreichung war es im Kot nicht mehr nachweisbar. Auch die von Clostridium immunis in eine Nährlösung abgegebenen Substanzen konnten jedoch das viszerale Fett der Mäuse verringern.

Als wirksame Substanz identifizierte das Team einen aus vielen Zuckerbausteinen bestehenden Mehrfachzucker, ein sogenanntes Exopolysaccharid (EPS). Es enthält vor allem Mannose und Glukose sowie einen chemischen Zusatz namens Phosphocholin. Die Gabe des isolierten Mehrfachzuckers reproduzierte die Effekte des Bakteriums auf Gewicht, Blutfette und viszerales Fett.

Entscheidend dafür ist die Phosphocholin-Gruppe, wie weitere Versuche mit genetisch veränderten Bakterien ergaben. Fehlte dem Mehrfachzucker diese chemische Gruppe, blieb die Wirkung aus. Auch freies Phosphocholin allein hatte keinen nachweisbaren Effekt auf die viszeralen Fettdepots.

### Eine Bremse der Fettverbrennung löst sich

Doch wie wirkt der bakterielle Zucker? Die Analysen enthüllten, dass Clostridium immunis die Zahl bestimmter Zellen des angeborenen Immunsystems im Darm verringert. Sowohl das Bakterium als auch sein Mehrfachzucker senken zudem den Gehalt des Immunbotenstoffs Interleukin-22 (IL-22) im Dünndarm und im viszeralen Fettgewebe.

Dadurch entstehen im viszeralen Fett vermehrt Zellen mit dem Protein UCP1, das bei der Umwandlung von Energie in Wärme eine Rolle spielt. Tatsächlich verbrauchten die Mäuse nach der Behandlung mit dem bakteriellen Zucker mehr Energie, und ihr isoliertes viszerales Fettgewebe zeigte einen erhöhten Sauerstoffverbrauch. Die Tiere fraßen dabei nicht weniger und bewegten sich auch nicht mehr als unbehandelte Artgenossen.

Dass der Immunbotenstoff für diesen Effekt entscheidend ist, bestätigten weitere Experimente. War IL-22 bereits durch Antikörper neutralisiert, konnte das Bakterium die viszeralen Fettpolster nicht weiter reduzieren. Umgekehrt schwächte die zusätzliche Gabe von IL-22 die Wirkung des Mehrfachzuckers auf das Fettgewebe ab. Wie viel der erhöhten Stoffwechselaktivität auf UCP1 selbst zurückgeht, ist allerdings noch offen.

### Wirkt der Zucker auch beim Menschen?

Erste Hinweise auf einen ähnlichen Zusammenhang beim Menschen liefert eine Auswertung von Darmflora-Daten von 4.145 Personen aus elf Studien. Demnach kamen bakterielle Kopien des an der Phosphocholin-Herstellung beteiligten Gens licC bei Menschen mit Adipositas in geringerer Zahl vor als bei Personen mit einem Body-Mass-Index unter 25. Auch bei einer separaten Analyse der Daten von 247 Menschen waren erhöhte Triglyceridwerte mit einer geringeren Häufigkeit dieses Gens assoziiert.

Ob der bakterielle Mehrfachzucker auch beim Menschen viszerales Fett abbauen kann, ist damit aber noch nicht erwiesen. Zudem waren die Zusammenhänge in den menschlichen Daten eher schwach. Ob das bakterielle Produkt eine Ergänzung zu bestehenden Therapien sein könnte, sollen daher klinische Untersuchungen klären.

> „GLP-1-Medikamente haben die Behandlung von Adipositas und ihren Begleiterkrankungen grundlegend verändert, doch sie wirken nicht bei jedem und verursachen oft erhebliche Nebenwirkungen“, erklärt Neeraj K. Surana.

Der Vorteil eines solchen neuen Ansatzes könnte darin liegen, gezielt die Stoffwechselaktivität des gesundheitlich besonders problematischen Fettgewebes zu erhöhen. Das Team hat bereits eine Patentanmeldung zur therapeutischen Nutzung der untersuchten Substanzen eingereicht und plant klinische Studien in den USA. Ob die Behandlung sicher und wirksam ist, muss sich dort erst zeigen.

**Quellen:**

- Originalstudie im Fachmagazin [Cell Host & Microbe](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chom.2026.08.018), doi: 10.1016/j.chom.2026.08.018
- Offizielle Studienmitteilung von [Duke University School of Medicine](https://medschool.duke.edu/news/sweet-discovery-fight-obesity)
- Offizielle Studienmitteilung von [Duke-NUS Medical School](https://www.duke-nus.edu.sg/newshub/media-releases/gut-sugar-may-help-body-burn-visceral-fat)

items.body:
**KARLSRUHE. Erneut geht die Bundesanwaltschaft gegen eine mutmaßliche rechtsextremistische Terrorgruppe vor, deren Mitglieder zum großen Teil noch im schulpflichtigen Alter sind. Wie der „Spiegel“ berichtet, wurden am Mittwoch drei Jugendliche im Alter von 14 und 15 Jahren festgenommen. Sie sollen sich über Chatgruppen in kürzester Zeit radikalisiert und schwerste Gewalttaten geplant haben. Bereits im vergangenen Jahr hatten Ermittlungen gegen eine andere rechtsextremistische Gruppierung mit überwiegend jungen Mitgliedern bundesweit für Aufsehen gesorgt.**

Die Polizei ermittelt (Symbolfoto). Foto: Shutterstock

Die Bundesanwaltschaft ermittelt[dem „Spiegel“ zufolge](https://www.spiegel.de/panorama/justiz/terror-18-bundesanwaltschaft-geht-gegen-mutmassliche-rechtsterroristen-vor-a-0f1adf41-8cf7-4306-934d-6d8d9186fa43) gegen insgesamt sechs Jugendliche und Heranwachsende im Alter von 14 bis 19 Jahren wegen des Verdachts der Mitgliedschaft in einer rechtsterroristischen Vereinigung. Die Gruppe soll sich aus einem rechtsextremistischen Chatgruppen-Netzwerk namens „Terror 18“ entwickelt haben. Die Zahl 18 steht in der Neonazi-Szene für die Initialen Adolf Hitlers.

Die Beschuldigten hätten sich „extrem schnell radikalisiert“, zitiert das Nachrichtenmagazin die Bundesanwaltschaft. Sie sollen Angriffe auf Geflüchtetenunterkünfte bis hin zu „gezielten Tötungen von Ausländern und politischen Gegnern“ geplant haben. Weitere Ermittlungen richten sich gegen vier Personen aus dem Umfeld der Gruppe. Auch bei einem Jungen in Brandenburg wurde dem Bericht zufolge eine Hausdurchsuchung vorgenommen. Gegen ihn wird allerdings nicht ermittelt: Er ist noch keine 14 Jahre alt und damit nicht strafmündig.

Bereits im Mai 2025 hatte die Bundesanwaltschaft fünf mutmaßliche Mitglieder der rechtsextremistischen Terrorgruppe „Letzte Verteidigungswelle“ festnehmen lassen. Auch sie waren erst zwischen 14 und 18 Jahre alt. Die Gruppierung wollte durch Gewalt gegen Migranten und politische Gegner die demokratische Ordnung destabilisieren.

Im August dieses Jahres verurteilte das Hanseatische Oberlandesgericht in Hamburg sieben Mitglieder und einen Unterstützer der Gruppe zu Freiheitsstrafen zwischen anderthalb und fünf Jahren – unter anderem wegen versuchten Mordes. Die Angeklagten waren zur Tatzeit zwischen 14 und 21 Jahre alt. Wie die Deutsche Presse-Agentur (dpa) im September berichtete, hat die Bundesanwaltschaft mittlerweile auch gegen zwei weitere Jugendliche aus dem Umfeld der Gruppe Anklage erhoben. *News4teachers / mit Material der dpa*

items.title: AI-generated video falsely shared as Crimean Bridge damage
items.subtitle: The fake footage doesn’t match official photos of the bridge, and Google says the clip contains a SynthID watermark.
items.feedText: A video shows damage caused to the Crimean Bridge after Ukrainian strikes in November 2026. This video isn’t real and was made with AI. A viral video supposedly showing damage to the Crimean Bridge after it was attacked by Ukraine in November 2026 isn’t real and was made with AI. The structure in the fake clip doesn’t match the real bridge, and Google’s SynthID detector told us the video contained an invisible SynthID watermark which suggests that it was made or edited with Google AI. The video has been 'liked' thousands of times online. It was first shared by an Instagram account on 16 November with claims it showed the damage caused by an initial drone attack .
items.body:
# AI-generated video falsely shared as Crimean Bridge damage – Full Fact

## AI-generated video falsely shared as Crimean Bridge damage

## What was claimed

A video shows damage caused to the Crimean Bridge after Ukrainian strikes in November 2026.

## Our verdict

False. This video isn’t real and was made with AI.

A viral video supposedly showing damage to the Crimean Bridge after it was attacked by Ukraine in November 2026 isn’t real and was made with AI.

The structure in the fake clip doesn’t match the real bridge, and Google’s SynthID detector told us the video contained an invisible SynthID watermark which suggests that it was made or edited with Google AI.

The video has been 'liked' thousands of times online. It was first shared by an Instagram account on 16 November with claims it showed the damage caused by an initial drone attack .

The first attack on 16 November reportedly damaged the arch over the road section of the bridge, but the fake footage does not match what the real bridge looks like.

Join 75,000 newsletter subscribers who trust us to check the facts

Sign up to get weekly updates on politics, immigration, health and more.

Subscribe to weekly email newsletters from Full Fact for updates on politics, immigration, health and more. Our fact checks are free to read but not to produce, so you will also get occasional emails about fundraising and other ways you can help. You can unsubscribe at any time. For more information about how we use your data see our Privacy Policy .

The fake version shows two road bridges. In reality , one of the bridges is a rail bridge . The real rail bridge arch also has a distinct criss-cross pattern on the lowest rung near the track that isn’t present in the fake version.

Ukraine attacked the bridge, which links occupied Crimea to Russia, again on 17 November, severing the road bridge , and on 19 November , reportedly damaging the rail bridge too.

Again, official photos of the damage caused by these later strikes do not match the fake video circulating online.

It can be difficult to tell the difference between real and AI-generated videos, particularly when they circulate after real events. Our misinformation toolkit can help you become more confident to spot AI-generated content.

Tags

This article is part of our work fact checking potentially false pictures, videos and stories on Facebook. You can read more about this—and find out how to report Facebook content— here . For the purposes of that scheme, we’ve rated this claim as altered because this video isn’t real and was made with AI.

## Was this helpful?

Full Fact fights for good, reliable information in the media, online, and in politics.

## Art Basel Announces New Highlights To Look Forward to at 2026 Miami Beach

[↗ Primärquelle: mymodernmet.com](https://mymodernmet.com/art-basel-miami-beach-2026-highlights/)

Art Basel Miami Beach, General Impressions, Courtesy of Art Basel

[Art Basel Miami Beach](https://mymodernmet.com/art-basel-miami-beach-2025-recap/) is preparing to bring the international art world together for another year. The fair has announced additional details for its 2026 edition, including major gallery presentations, digital art projects, artist conversations, and public installations throughout South Florida. With 272 exhibitors from more than 40 countries and territories, the event will offer a wide-ranging look at contemporary art and the ideas shaping it.

The newly announced gallery presentations span several generations and mediums. Brazilian artist Rosana Paulino will present her first bronze sculpture, *Crisálida* (2025–26), with Mendes Wood DM. Other highlights include a new painting by Shara Hughes at David Kordansky Gallery and monumental bronze sculpture by Wangechi Mutu at Gladstone. A joint presentation by Ortuzar and Crèvecœur will feature paintings by Ernie Barnes, coinciding with an exhibition of his work at ICA Miami. Miami-based Spinello Projects will also make its debut in the Galleries sector, showcasing artists from the Latin American and Caribbean diaspora.

Digital art will have an expanded presence through Zero 10: Generation, the initiative’s largest edition to date. Curated by Karen Archey and Eli Scheinman, it brings together 21 exhibitors across 19 projects. The presentations explore generative art, artificial intelligence, and emerging technologies. The program also looks to the history of digital experimentation, with a presentation on early computer art in Latin America and a new collaboration with Google Arts & Culture.

The fair’s Conversations program will explore the connections between art and other cultural fields, including sports and technology. Across four days, artists, curators, and public figures will discuss topics ranging from creative practice to identity and representation.

A dedicated Art & Sports series features NBA champion Kevin Love, soccer star Crystal Dunn, and Brooklyn Nets and New York Liberty co-owner Clara Wu Tsai. The program also includes a panel with the NFL examining portraiture and legacy in professional football.

Beyond the convention center, public art and museum exhibitions will extend the experience across Greater Miami. In Collins Park, *Between Tides*, a collaboration with Public Art Fund, transforms six ping-pong tables into playable sculptural installations designed by artists.

The Art Basel Awards will also return for a second year, recognizing achievements across the contemporary art world. The winners will be announced at a ceremony at Miami Beach’s New World Center.

Art Basel Miami Beach takes place Dec. 4–6, at the Miami Beach Convention Center. VIP preview days are scheduled for December 2–3.

Every month, we share opportunities for artists and designers, including open calls, grants, fellowships, and residencies. Make sure you never miss out by joining our monthly [Opportunities Newsletter](https://www.thisiscolossal.com/newsletter/opportunities/).

**[Fall $1,800 Innovate Grants for Art + Photo](https://innovateartistgrants.org)** **Featured**
Innovate Grant awards two $1,800 grants each quarter to one visual artist and one photographer. Nine honorable mentions in each category are also featured on the Innovate Grant platform and join a growing creative community of esteemed artists. Applicants must be 18 years and older, and all media and genres are accepted. All applicants retain the right to the work they submit.
**Deadline: 11:59 p.m. PST on December 15, 2026.**

**[Bryson County Retreat](https://www.brysoncountyretreat.org/)** **Featured**
Practicing artists of any background and at any stage of their career are encouraged to apply for a 2027 residency at Bryson County Retreat. Residency periods can be flexible, but month-long stays are suggested. Bryson County is designed to provide ample living and working space and inspirational settings where an artist may work free from the distractions and responsibilities of day-to-day life. The program includes free lodging near tannic dark water lakes, sprawling live oaks, and drooping Spanish moss at the headwaters of the Santa Fe River in north central Florida.
**Deadline: Rolling.**

**Open Calls**

**[Wildlife Photographer of the Year](https://www.nhm.ac.uk/wildlife-photographer-of-the-year/competition.html)** *(International)*
Alongside its conservation message, this prestigious global competition is hosted by London’s Natural History Museum to champion the work of photographers, whether professional or amateur, young or older, or using top-of-the-range equipment or smartphones. Photographers are eligible for myriad awards, with a Grand Title prize of £15,000. The entry fee is £35 (free for Young WPY contest).
**Deadline: 11:30 p.m. GMT on December 3, 2026.**

**[Responsa Foundation Open Call for Textile Art](https://responsafoundation.com/2026/10/13/this-memory-competition/)** *(International)*
The Responsa Foundation champions projects that create meaningful social impact and foster public engagement. The organization is seeking textile artists to submit work for *This Memory,* a group exhibition taking place from September 22 to October 3, 2027, at Burgh House in Hampstead.
**Deadline: December 4, 2026.**

**[Open Call for Public Art Proposals in Moab](https://www.moabarts.org/public-art-application)** (Utah, National)
Moab Arts is accepting proposals for 2027 public art projects. Proposals are welcome for sculpture, murals, three crosswalks, and sticker designs but may include other ideas for different media or locations around the city. Preference is given to local and regional artists.
**Deadline: 11:59 p.m. MST on December 6, 2026.**

**[Material Works Art Award 2026](https://pci.jotform.com/form/262185636090156)** *(International)*
Material Works supports artists through one-time $2,500 awards in exchange for original pieces added to its growing contemporary art collection. The award recognizes artistic excellence and aims to promote career advancement through increasing visibility and exposure. There is a €40 application fee.
**Deadline: December 6, 2026, or when the first 300 artworks submitted, whichever comes first.**

**[Call for Mail Art](https://www.hivebookarts.org/exhibitions/call-for-mail-art)** *(International)*
Hive Center for the Book Arts in Evanston, Illinois, welcomes mail art for the exhibition *love|mark*, which runs from January 1 to February 27. All submissions must arrive at at the center by December 15 for inclusion in the show.
**Deadline:** **December 15, 2026.**

**[Sony Future Filmmaker Awards](https://www.sonyfuturefilmmakerawards.com/)** *(International)*
The Sony Future Filmmaker Awards is a major program providing opportunities for creators and filmmakers. The shortlisted filmmakers are flown to Sony Pictures Studios in Culver City, California, to attend an awards ceremony and an industry immersion program. Categories include fiction, nonfiction, animation, immersive, student, and vertical format.
**Deadline: 7 a.m. CST on December 15, 2026.**

**[GLEAM 2027 Request for Proposals](https://www.olbrichgleam.org/submit-a-proposal)** *(International)*
Olbrich Botanical Gardens in Madison, Wisconsin, invites proposals for temporary, large-scale, light-based artwork for *GLEAM*, a public art exhibition. The show will be open to the public from August 28 to October 23, 2027.
**Deadline: 11:59 p.m. CST on January 6, 2027.**

**[Visual Arts Prize IDEA – Vila d’Amer](https://www.ideagc.com/en/idea-mundoarti/)** *(International)*
Apply for this inaugural prize open to artists working in all visual arts media. Two winning artworks, with prizes of €3,500 and €1,500, will become part of the permanent International Visual Arts Collection IDEA – Vila d’Amer.
**Deadline: January 10, 2027.**

**[360 CHICAGO: CloudWalk Call for Artists](https://360chicago.com/cloudwalk-call-for-artists)** *(Chicago)*
One artist will be selected for this major installation in the CloudWalk gallery atop 875 N. Michigan Ave. The selected artist receives a $10,000 commission, and the winning installation will go on view starting April 2027.
**Deadline: January 18, 2027.**

**[World of WearableArt 2027 Competition](https://www.worldofwearableart.com/competition/entry-information)** *(International)*
Entries are now open for the 2027 WOW Competition in Wellington, New Zealand. Awards consist of NZ$200,000 in prizes, including the Supreme WOW Award of NZ$30,000.
**Deadline: February 11, 2027 (international), March 31, 2027 (New Zealand).**

**Grants**

**[The Filmed in Nevada County Grant](https://nevadacityfilmfestival.com/filmedinnc/)** *(International)*
To support filmmakers in the production of work in Nevada County, California, Nevada City Film Festival offers grants between $1,000 and $20,000.
**Deadline: December 1, 2026.**

**[Southern Prize and State Fellowships for Visual Arts](https://www.southarts.org/grants-opportunities/southern-prize-and-state-fellowships-visual-arts)** *(U.S. South)*
The South Arts Southern Prize and State Fellowships acknowledge the highest quality artistic work being created in the American South. The program is open to individual artists living in Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Louisiana, Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina, and Tennessee. State Fellowships are $5,000, with one awarded per state. These then compete for two Southern Prize tiers of $25,000 and $10,000.
**Deadline: January 15, 2027 (fee waiver request by December 18, 2026).**

items.body:
A large light well brings daylight deep into this private [home](https://www.dezeen.com/tag/houses/) that was designed by [Desai Chia Architecture](https://www.dezeen.com/tag/desai-chia-architecture/) for a tight site in a dense [Maryland](https://www.dezeen.com/tag/maryland/) neighbourhood.

The project takes its name from its location in Bethesda, a city located northwest of Washington DC.

The house is set within a suburban neighbourhood near the downtown district, where residential lots are about one-fifth of an acre (647 square metres). Because the houses here are close together, the architects needed to be very mindful of privacy concerns.

### Drawings and photographs

Previous

Next

### Drawings and photographs

Close

- Basement and first floor plans
- Second and third floor plans
- Roof plan

“The clients sought a house that would feel open and light-filled without sacrificing privacy,” said New York-based [Desai Chia Architecture](https://www.desaichia.com/).

“Its compact lot and the close proximity of neighbouring houses required a careful response balancing both openness and discretion."

The architects intended the house to “rethink suburban-urban hybrid living through a modern lens”.

Roughly rectangular in plan, it has three levels and a basement. Setbacks help break up the mass, particularly on the street-facing elevation.

The building appears “as a two-storey building from several vantage points,” the team said.

“The home is carefully scaled to blend with neighbouring houses, balancing a strong architectural identity with sensitivity to its suburban context,” the team said.

Facades are clad in grey fibre-cement panels made to last for a century. The material is known for protecting against fire, pests and extreme weather, according to the team.

“A durable, low-maintenance exterior with a strong architectural presence was a key client priority from the outset,” the architects said.

“Glass-fibre-reinforced concrete (GRFC) panels were selected to create a crisp, sculptural facade that captures texture and shifting light throughout the day.”

[Read: Desai Chia uses "camouflaging effect" for secluded Osprey House in New York](https://www.dezeen.com/2025/11/27/desai-chia-camouflaging-effect-osprey-house-new-york/)

A modern-style bay window adds dimension and visual interest to the front and back facades.

Within the home, public spaces are located on the ground level. The rear portion opens into a yard with a lap pool.

The upper levels contain bedrooms and two offices, and the top floor has a rooftop terrace. The basement holds a gym, ping-pong area and media room.

A limited number of windows helps ensure privacy. To provide natural illumination, the team created a three-storey light well, which is positioned along a central staircase and brings daylight deep into the dwelling.

“This vertical, faceted volume allows sunlight to cascade downward, distributing diffuse light from a small skylight across circulation spaces on multiple levels while minimising solar heat gain,” Desai Chia Architecture said.

The all-electric house has a geothermal heating and cooling system. To enable the homeowners to age in place, the house has a shaft where an ADA-compliant elevator could be added in the future.

The homeowners are physicians, one of whom can walk to his practice in downtown Bethesda.

“When needed, the dedicated home offices allow both physicians to work from home in spaces with calming natural light,” the studio said.

“Its location – easily walkable to downtown amenities and robust public transit – supports a connected pattern of work and family life.”

Other homes in Maryland include a [restored carriage house by Colleen Healey Architecture](https://www.dezeen.com/2022/06/09/colleen-healey-red-maple-house-maryland/) that features colourful facade panels and a [family home by Ziger Snead](https://www.dezeen.com/2018/08/27/slate-house-ziger-snead-architects-replaces-fire-ravaged-home-maryland/) clad in stone shingles, charred wood and weathering steel.

**Project credits:**

**Design architect:** Desai Chia Architecture
**Architect of record:** Thomson & Cooke Architects

items.body:
*Piaget’s second collaboration with The Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts translates the pop artist’s 1986 Camouflage self-portraits into dials made of gemstone marquetry.*

## Related Articles

### What Is Internet Cinema?

[↗ Primärquelle: artnews.com](https://www.artnews.com/art-news/artists/what-is-internet-cinema-1234807781/)

### Christie's Adds UK Auction House Dreweatts to Its Portfolio

[↗ Primärquelle: artnews.com](https://www.artnews.com/art-news/market/christies-adds-uk-auction-house-dreweatts-to-portfolio-1234807665/)

Long before luxury watches were as sought after as they are today, Andy Warhol coveted and collected them. Over the course of the 1960s, ’70s, and ’80s, the Pop Art pioneer amassed more than 300 timepieces that reflected his high-low tastes. He collected watches the way he collected everything, with an appetite that blurred connoisseurship and compulsion. When Sotheby’s sold his estate in 1988, the sale featured timepieces by Cartier, Bulgari, and Patek Philippe alongside cookie jars and Art Deco furniture. Warhol is often said to have worn watches less to tell time than to be seen in them. For an artist who made a career of elevating the ordinary, a watch was a portable piece of pop culture, a status symbol he could wear and treasure.

Photo Courtesy of Piaget

One brand, however, stood out. Warhol owned at least seven wristwatches by the Swiss maison, Piaget. Founded in 1874 in La Côte-aux-Fées, a village in the heart of Switzerland’s Jura mountain range, the house was renowned in the latter half of the 20th century for its creative selection of timepieces in unusual shapes, many featuring dials made of exotic ornamental stones. One of those watches, a quartz-powered reference 15102 model that Warhol purchased from the brand in 1973, now forms the foundation for a Piaget collection bound to appeal to lovers of art in general and fans of Warhol’s revolutionary oeuvre in particular.

Housed in an 18-karat gold, 45 mm cushion-shaped case designed by Jean-Claude Gueit, Piaget’s then artistic director, the striking piece, which was part of a limited series manufactured between 1972 and 1977, featured a black onyx dial. Fittingly, it was called the Black Tie. In 1988, Piaget purchased Warhol’s watch at Sotheby’s landmark sale.

Photo Courtesy of Piaget

The artist’s choice of Piaget was no accident. In the 1950s and ’60s, the house had built its reputation on extreme thinness, introducing ultra-thin movements that transformed the watches into slim, supple pieces of jewelry. By the 1960s, Piaget had paired that technical prowess with a bolder sensibility: gold bracelets, vivid hardstone dials, and silhouettes that owed more to the jeweler’s bench than to the watchmaker’s. The result was a crossover brand that suited the decade’s appetite for spectacle. For Warhol, who drew no line between commerce and art, a watch that doubled as a gem-set object was irresistible. The Black Tie’s onyx dial, as sleek and dark as a lacquered cigarette case, could not have been better suited to the man who documented the era’s elite so closely.

Twenty-six years after Piaget purchased the Black Tie, the brand used the occasion of its 140th anniversary in 2014 to create a revival collection called Black Tie Vintage. The line caused such a stir among Piaget’s clientele that in 2024, for its sesquicentennial, the maison decided to up the ante. Thanks to a collaboration with The Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts, Piaget was given the rights to rename the Black Tie Vintage watch after Warhol himself.

**From Collage to Camouflage**

The first collaborative watch to emerge from Piaget’s work with the foundation was the 2025 Collage, a limited edition of 50 pieces featuring an artful composition of ornamental stones—yellow Namibian serpentine, pink opal, and green chrysoprase—inspired by Warhol’s Polaroids. This month, Piaget has introduced a second piece, which also uses ornamental stone marquetry, this time to pay tribute to the *Camouflage* self-portraits that Warhol created in 1986.

Photo Courtesy of Piaget

“When you buy it, you don’t only buy a watch, you buy a whole story and heritage,” Jean-Bernard Forot, Piaget’s head of patrimony, tells *ARTnews*. “You can, of course, talk about the material, what it does for you. But at the same time, you have to talk about Warhol, you have to talk about Piaget, you have to talk about art.”

Limited to 86 pieces, after the year in which Warhol created the eight-print *Camouflage* series, the watch, whose dial combines the ornamental stones sodalite and turquoise with satin-finished yellow gold and polished rose gold, faithfully interprets the artist’s work without blindly mimicking it.

“Camouflage is very difficult to work on, even in design, because we don’t just copy and paste the artwork—we have to find another way to express camouflage,” Forot says.

Among the final serial group of paintings Warhol completed before his untimely death in 1987, the works paid homage to the military-inspired camouflage pattern, originally intended to help soldiers blend in with their surroundings. In Warhol’s hands, they became a comment on Abstract Expressionism, not to mention a deeply personal statement on his lifelong effort to conceal his true self beneath wigs, makeup, and a carefully constructed facade.

Photo Courtesy of Piaget

Printed in acid brights across enormous canvases, the swirling forms feature in self-portraits overlayed with Warhol’s face, framed by his signature shock of hair. For an artist who spent his life hiding in plain sight, the *Camouflage* series is arguably his most meta work.

In order to capture the essence of the paintings on the face of a watch, Piaget’s artisans took some liberties with color. Rather than emphasizing Warhol’s use of yellow, for example, they highlighted the brand’s use of turquoise, Forot says.

“Once the team finished the drawing, which was validated by The Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts, then they started working with the gem material,” he says. “We have to try to remain true to both the design itself as well as the techniques.”

**Mad About Hue**

Study the dial of the watch and you’ll see something of an optical illusion: a sense of depth and texture that isn’t quite there. “When you look at the Piaget Camouflage, you have the feeling that you have four layers,” Forot says. “But in fact, it’s an illusion because they are all flat and on the same level. Even if you have the feeling that the turquoise is above the gold, in fact, it’s at the same level.”

Photo Courtesy of Piaget

items.body:
On the northwestern tip of France's Noirmoutier Island, behind the 19th-century Church of the Sacred Heart, a small cemetery overlooks the Atlantic Ocean. Beyond its stone walls stretch the waters of the Bay of Biscay, with the tiny island of Le Pilier visible on the horizon. Many of those buried here were sailors and fishermen whose lives were intimately connected to the sea.

Among the traditional graves stands a striking row of white Commonwealth headstones, commemorating the victims of a largely forgotten maritime tragedy.

On June 17, 1940, as British troops and civilians were being evacuated from France, German aircraft bombed the British troopship HMT Lancastria off the coast of Saint-Nazaire. The ship sank within minutes, taking thousands of lives in one of the deadliest maritime disasters of World War II.

In the following days, the Atlantic currents carried the bodies of victims onto the French coastline, including the shores of Noirmoutier.

Today, the cemetery contains 40 Commonwealth war burials, 22 of them unidentified. Most were victims of the Lancastria disaster.

Overlooking the very ocean that claimed so many lives, L'Herbaudière's marine cemetery remains a peaceful yet poignant reminder of the island's maritime heritage and the tragedies of war.

items.body:
## STUDIO MASSIMO EMBEDS TIMBER OFFICE INTO DUTCH HEATHLAND

Situated on the Tafelberg heath in Blaricum, east of **[Amsterdam](https://www.designboom.com/tag/architecture-in-the-netherlands/)**, Office by Nature, Tafelberg is a 1,120-sqm**[timber](https://www.designboom.com/tag/wood-and-timber-architecture/) [office](https://www.designboom.com/tag/where-people-work/)**designed by Studio Massimo. Built within a protected glacial landscape and drinking-water catchment area, the project required low-impact construction to protect the surrounding soil. Taking structural and formal cues from the regional plaggenhut, a traditional earthen-walled dwelling topped with a sod roof, the building merges directly with the terrain. The ground slopes upward without an edge or material break to form a walkable living**[roof](https://www.designboom.com/tag/rooftop-architecture-and-design/)** planted with more than one hundred native, organically grown species.

Each elevation responds to its orientation. On the north side facing the road, the planted slope terminates at a mortarless retaining wall of stacked reclaimed paving tiles, punctuated only by a timber entrance door. The east and west gables are clad in untreated poplar bark shingles, a timber-industry byproduct that weathers from umber to silver-gray, while six-meter-wide sliding glass doors on the south facade open the workspaces directly onto the heath.

the office seen from the Tafelberg heath | all images ©Riccardo De Vecchi

## CLT STRUCTURE and RED GRANDIS INTERIORS COMPLETE BUILDING

Constructed from a laminated timber and cross-laminated timber (CLT) frame insulated with wood fiber, the interior is finished in a continuous palette of Red Grandis timber across walls, ceilings, doors, and joinery, with ventilation slots milled directly into the wood panels to eliminate visible grilles. A seven-meter-high central hall illuminated by an overhead skylight anchors the plan, floored in terrazzo aggregate containing split Kunrader stone from South Limburg, the same stone used for the exterior plinth. The design studio integrates a rainwater harvesting system that treats and reuses runoff for roof irrigation and toilets, guiding water down the south facade via reused crane chains, where each bay incorporates a secondary, higher overflow chain that discharges only when gutters require clearing. Outside, a sunken seating area built from reclaimed mooring poles and glacial boulders sits within untamed native planting.

items.feedText: It’s worth taking a moment to appreciate how surprising this is — given enough tries, the same learning process turned every novice into an expert light seeker. Of the myriad possible arrangements of this spark’s brain, only a tiny fraction generate the behavior that we want. There are far more ways to fail than to succeed. And yet, you’ve just witnessed a small miracle. The spark navigated this labyrinth of dead ends and rewired its brain to find the light, guided by nothing but reward and punishment. Tags: Aat…
items.body:
Continuing their series on how our brains find the right paths, Aatish Bhatia and Arkarup Banerjee show the learning process through “sparks” that stand in as simplified versions of brains [moving through a space of possible brains](https://aatishb.com/myriad/how-brains-learn/).

> It’s worth taking a moment to appreciate how surprising this is — given enough tries, the same learning process turned every novice into an expert light seeker.
> Of the myriad possible arrangements of this spark’s brain, only a tiny fraction generate the behavior that we want. There are far more ways to fail than to succeed.
> And yet, you’ve just witnessed a small miracle. The spark navigated this labyrinth of dead ends and rewired its brain to find the light, guided by nothing but reward and punishment.

**Tags:** [Aatish Bhatia](https://flowingdata.com/tag/aatish-bhatia/), [Arkarup Banerjee](https://flowingdata.com/tag/arkarup-banerjee/), [brain](https://flowingdata.com/tag/brain/), [learning](https://flowingdata.com/tag/learning/)

items.body:
## Photographer Shares the Emotional Story Behind an Elephant Carrying Its Stillborn Calf [Interview]

[↗ Primärquelle: mymodernmet.com](https://mymodernmet.com/federico-veronesi-wildlife-photography/)

“The Aftermath”

Wildlife photographer [Federico Veronesi](https://federicoveronesi.com/) encountered the shot of a lifetime in Damaraland, Namibia. In September 2025, he witnessed a desert elephant carrying its stillborn calf. What resulted was an arresting black-and-white image that is beautifully composed but ultimately full of grief. The close-up portrait shows the mother with her deceased calf between her tusk and trunk, as if she is unable to let her baby go. The emotional image, titled *The Aftermath*, was recognized in the prestigious [Wildlife Photographer of the Year 2026 competition](https://mymodernmet.com/natural-history-museum-wildlife-photographer-of-the-year-2026/), with Veronesi earning the title of Overall Winner and the Behavior Mammals category winner.

Veronesi was tracking elephants when he noticed an unusual pattern of drag marks in the sand of a dry riverbed. He understood why when he saw the mother and child. “The calf’s body rose up and in this particular frame, it almost looks like the calf is still alive, playing with its mother or trying to cling to her mother’s trunk,” he recalls to My Modern Met. “I feel that the ambiguity of the image, and how it can be read in many ways make it stand out from the other images I took, where the calf is clearly hanging lifeless from the mother’s tusk.”

The photographer initially felt conflicted about capturing the scene. “After taking the first few images, I felt like I was violating the elephant’s intimate moment, her grief, I was almost ashamed and thought that I shouldn’t take these photographs,” he shares. But ultimately, Veronesi found it important to highlight the complexity of these creatures. Elephants have been observed engaging in behaviors around death, including vocalizing, guarding the deceased, and carrying the dead, as pictured. By photographing this painful moment, Veronesi shows us that wildlife and humans aren’t as far apart as we may think.

We spoke with Veronesi about capturing the poignant shot, his philosophy about photographing wildlife, and more. Scroll down for My Modern Met’s exclusive interview.

**What is your photography background, and how did you begin photographing wildlife?**

Photography was part of my life since an early age as I grew up in a family of keen nature photographers. Every travel or outing was always centered on photographing nature, birds and wildlife in particular. I therefore learned photography almost naturally. I began photographing wildlife with my Polaroid on my first trip to Africa when I was 6 years old or to the local zoos and safari parks. During my teenage years I upgraded to a reflex camera and slides, and that’s what I used for my first years in Kenya after I moved there in 2002 to follow my dream of living among wildlife and photographing it full time.

**Set up the scene for your image The Aftermath, which shows an elephant carrying a dead calf. How did you come across this?**

I was in Damaraland, northwestern Namibia, with the specific aim to photograph desert-adapted elephants and other wildlife living in this particularly dry but stunning ecosystem. Elephants are frequently found along the dry riverbeds that traverse this landscape, as that’s where they find some trees and vegetation that they can feed on. I had seen a family of elephants the previous evening, so that morning I returned to the place where I left them to pick up their tracks and hopefully find them again. As I followed the tracks, I noticed an unusual dragging mark on the ground, which I wasn’t immediately able to interpret. Shortly after I finally came across the elephants feeding on the river banks. Out of the group, a female appeared carrying a dead calf by wedging the calf’s leg between her trunk and tusk.

**How did the final image emerge? Did you realize the photograph’s importance when you snapped it?**

As the scene appeared in front of me, I grabbed my 400mm telephoto lens and framed the images, I went for a vertical crop as she was coming towards me and she filled the frame nicely. As she came forward, another elephant was following her, so she abruptly turned away. The calf’s body rose up and in this particular frame, it almost looks like the calf is still alive, playing with its mother or trying to cling to her mother’s trunk. I feel that the ambiguity of the image, and how it can be read in many ways make it stand out from the other images I took, where the calf is clearly hanging lifeless from the mother’s tusk. After taking the first few images I felt like I was violating the elephant’s intimate moment, her grief, I was almost ashamed and thought that I shouldn’t take these photographs. However, as I reflected on the event, I realized how important it was for me to tell the story, to offer people an open window into the soul of the elephant, into her feelings, into her memories, hopefully to make people understand the complexity of the animals’ emotions and sensibility. That’s why I also chose black and white, to expose these emotions without any possible distraction.

**What is your philosophy when photographing wildlife? **

When I am photographing wildlife, I am always looking for images where I can reveal how similar we are to them on an emotional level, and to establish a connection on the emotional level. I like to try to tell their story, and our story through them somehow. I strive to make images where people can see themselves in the animals. All of this while never disturbing the animals, never altering their behavior, and never manipulating my images digitally.

**What can it tell us about our own humanity?**

It’s fascinating to realize how much in common we have with the animals, how much our own behaviors can be interpreted in ecological terms and referred back to many of the behaviors that I witness in the wild. Some people’s lack of empathy towards animals is what I try to win over with my images, hoping that this can result in more efforts to peacefully coexist with wildlife, to not consider them only as disposable resources but sentient creatures that should be respected and protected. Sometimes I feel like our humanity is torn between people at war with our planet and its inhabitants, determined to exploit it to their benefit without any care for anything or anyone else, and those who are fighting to protect it. I hope to provide some tools in this battle with my images.

**You’ve recently won the prestigious Wildlife Photographer of the Year 2026 competition for The Aftermath. Congrats! What was it like to have your work recognized in this way?**

items.body:
Around the dusty plains and otherworldly volcanic rock formations of the historical region of [Cappadocia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cappadocia), a millennia-old tradition continues. Here in Central Anatolia, Turkey, horses have been a part of daily life, civic programs, and military campaigns since prehistory. In *[The Untold Story of the Yilki Horse](https://hemeria.com/en-us/products/the-untold-story-of-the-yilki-horses)*, photographer [Nur Tucker](https://nurtucker.com/) captures a portrait of the region’s living heritage.

Published by Hemeria, the title delves into the beauty and tenacity of the semi-wild horses while also highlighting the lifestyles of those who herd them through rugged landscapes. Tucker, who is a British-Turkish photographer based in the U.K., has long been drawn to the vigor and elegance of horses, and the [yilki breed](https://www.yilkiatlari.org.tr/en/history.html) that populates Anatolia have a particularly resonant history.

“Yilki” comes from the Turkish verb *yılmak*, which means “to flee” or “to be set loose.” The name “has come to describe the condition of these herds that live between liberation and loss, between domestic heritage and wild abandon,” says a statement.

In a place where horses have been bred for agriculture, transportation, battle, and more for thousands of years, their role forever changed within just the past century due to mechanization and industrialization. With motorized tractors, trucks, and cars to work the fields and provide transportation, horses essentially became redundant. Released to fend for themselves, they survived harsh winters, bred on their own, and grew into sizable herds. In *The Untold Story of the Yilki Horse,* Tucker composes a love letter to these striking animals, celebrating their resilience through more than 100 images.

The book is available for purchase directly from [Hemeria](https://hemeria.com/en-us/products/the-untold-story-of-the-yilki-horses), and it’s slated for worldwide release next October. See more on Tucker’s [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/nurtuckerphotography/?hl=en).

Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a [Colossal Member](https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members) today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. items.body:
London architecture practice Tuckey Design Studio has renovated and extended Bay House in rural Yorkshire, using a rich, moody palette intended to evoke the feeling of a wine bar.

The project involved reconfiguring and expanding the country house dating from the early 2000s, while introducing a garden spa and sauna.

Photographs

Previous

Next

Photographs

Close

Tuckey Design Studio was tasked by the clients to recreate the feeling of their favourite wine bar, which informed a palette of dark timber carpentry, terracotta-painted walls and a bespoke wine storage cabinet alongside a tasting area.

"The ambition was clear from the beginning: to bring the atmosphere of a much-loved London wine bar into the home," project lead Fraser Biggins told Dezeen.

"The clients’ enthusiasm for wine and music became important touchstones for the design, informing both the arrangement of the spaces and the character of the interiors," he added.

The home's previously cramped interiors are now centred on a large, double-height atrium, which serves as both a point of arrival and a gathering and tasting space with a bespoke timber "wine wall".

This hall is finished with dark timber panelling, terrazzo floors and terracotta paintwork, with a wall alongside an arched composite stone staircase punctured by small square openings.

This central space leads through into the social spaces, with a kitchen and dining space finished using similar dark timber panelling and concrete countertops.

The stairs lead up to the first floor via a landing with a built-in bench, where a balcony connecting the bedrooms enjoys views of the hall below. It also looks across the garden through windows in a new bay window extension.

"The central hall forms the organising principle of the house, providing a shared space from which the surrounding family rooms and activities unfold," Biggins told Dezeen.

"A series of interconnected spaces, galleries and overlooking balconies create visual connections across different levels, allowing the house to feel both connected and varied," he added.

On the first floor, two of the existing bedrooms have been converted into a games room and bar space, finished in dark shades of green and grey.

Alongside them are four ensuite bedrooms finished in warmer shades of pale pink and yellow, with each featuring a hand-painted mural designed to "reflect the character of each occupant".

"Material choices were guided by a desire for honesty, durability and longevity," Biggins told Dezeen.

"We wanted the spaces to feel timeless and comfortable, without relying too heavily on traditional materials or references."

Read:

Tuckey Design Studio restores original character of Old Chapel in Devon

"Instead, the palette brings together robust, tactile finishes that feel natural and lived-in, allowing the character of the materials to speak for themselves," he added.

The exterior of the extension has been finished in composite stone and dark accoya wood, and looks across the home's garden to the standalone spa and sauna, which was designed as a "complementary counterpoint" to the main home.

Previous projects by Tuckey Design Studio include a home in Wiltshire constructed using walls of unstabilised rammed earth and a residence within a converted chapel in Devon.
